surfaces.notes: ShareAddressLink :494-526 (doc-comment :486-493). Joins place.address/city/state/zipcode (:496), builds BuildConfig.PANTOPUS_WEB_BASE_URL + "/start?address=" + Uri.encode(address) (:502), fires Intent.ACTION_SEND through a chooser (:503-509), testTag "place.preview.share" (:512). gaps: Compare header: nothing anywhere reads a `vs` query param. grep for "vs=" across frontend/apps/web/src/app/start, src/components/place and src/app/api/og returns zero hits, and grep for compare-card/compareCard/COMPARE_CARD across backend/ and frontend/ returns zero hits. The sender-column header above the hero, the empty "Your place" column, and the `t0_compare_viewed` beacon are all net-new; the only precedent for a param-driven banner above the H1 is the from-card pill at StartFunnel.tsx:102-110.

Two-column reveal: the preview step is a single fixed-width column (StartFunnel.tsx:748, max-w-[480px]/sm:max-w-[540px]) while the hero is max-w-[1000px] with an lg two-column grid (:726, :100). PreviewBody (:398-457) emits one vertical stack and PreviewSkeleton (:547-574) is single-column, so a side-by-side sender/recipient reveal has no layout, no loading state, and no container to hang off.

Compare share affordance: ShareAddressLink (StartFunnel.tsx:490-517) is the only share control and it puts the raw address in the URL. There is no "Compare with a friend" button under the aha card, no `meta.method: 'compare'` path (the event is hard-coded to 'share'|'copy' at :498), and no compare sheet — so the optional "Show my first name on the card" field has no surface either.

Per-grade "how we know" lines: the four F8 chips (Flood / Wildfire / Air today / Radon) are assembled only inside the OG route (frontend/apps/web/src/app/api/og/place/route.tsx:61-66) and never rendered as a UI row. Web sections carry a single source/caption per card (presentation.tsx:498, :530; AhaCard.tsx:88) with no per-chip provenance string, and there is no "AirNow, today" / "FEMA flood zone" style attribution anywhere.

Expired/tampered-token banner: no token verification exists to fail. There is no POST/GET /api/public/compare-card route and backend/utils/homePostcardCodeMaterial.js (keyring at :10-25, deriveCode :37-50, exports :51) is the only HMAC keyring pattern — it is postcard-specific and has no compare-card analogue. The funnel's existing error states (CouldNotPlace :585-600, UnsupportedRegion :602-618, the isError branch :752-758) are all about the RECIPIENT's address, not about a bad inbound link.

OG vs-mode and caching: /api/og/place reads only `address` (route.tsx:45) and returns ImageResponse with no headers argument (:124) — no Cache-Control today, and no two-column "Yours?" layout. It also fetches the live preview with cache:'no-store' (:51), so a token-rendered card would need a different data path.

Funnel event types: `t0_compare_viewed` and `session_open` are absent from all four places that gate an event — the DB CHECK constraint (supabase/migrations/20260908234526_application_baseline.sql:9651, six values), backend/services/funnelEvents.js:33 and :48, frontend/packages/api/src/endpoints/funnel.ts:20-25, and backend/services/funnelReport.js:54,72 (no compare rate). The migration to mirror is backend/database/migrations/196_funnel_event_aha_share.sql.

Positioning-line constants: frontend/packages/types/src/copy.ts does not exist (the package ships ai.ts…wallet.ts and no copy module), so POSITIONING_LINE / POSITIONING_CONTRAST have nowhere to live. The line is duplicated verbatim at start/page.tsx:12, StartFunnel.tsx:114, HeroSection.tsx:41, PlaceLaunchView.swift:128 and PlaceLaunchScreen.kt:143, and the contrast line ("Nextdoor is what your neighbors say…") appears in no file, on no platform.

Rotating seasonal headline: pickAha(sections) takes sections only (placePreviewService.js:438) and is called with no context (public.js:560). There is no SEASONAL_HEADLINES table, no date/state parameter, and no AddressCalendarRule read anywhere in the anonymous path — the calm fallback (:456-469) and the AHA_BUILDERS ranking are the whole mechanism today.

Same-cell Founding line: the anonymous preview receives only a boolean. densityEnvelope emits founding_open (placePreviewService.js:191) from foundingSlotsOpen (public.js:549, foundingWindow.js:67-73) while the richer {slots_open, ends_at} exists but is exposed only on the signed-in block detail (blockFoundersService.js:336-344). WallBar (StartFunnel.tsx:520-544) takes two props and has no founding slot, no geohash, and no knowledge of a sender's cell. Also note public.js:557 defaults foundingOpen to TRUE on a failed lookup — fail-open, the opposite of the fail-closed rule F8 states.

iOS share/compare parity: PlacePreviewBody.swift has no share control at all — its wall (:314-331) is headline + Continue + 24-hour line. SystemShareSheet exists (SystemSheets.swift:48-59) but grep for ShareLink/UIActivityViewController under frontend/apps/ios/Pantopus/Features/Place/ returns nothing, so iOS is a step behind Android (which at least has ShareAddressLink at PlaceLaunchScreen.kt:494-526) before any compare work starts.

Native funnel instrumentation: grep for recordFunnelEvent / funnel-events / FunnelEvent across frontend/apps/ios/Pantopus and frontend/apps/android/app/src/main returns nothing. Neither native client records t0_preview_viewed, t0_aha_viewed or t0_share_clicked, so the F8 spread metric (compares sent ÷ aha views, doc line 42) is web-only by construction — and Android's existing ShareAddressLink (:502-509) fires no beacon while web's does (StartFunnel.tsx:498).

surfaces.name: POST /api/saved-places (the save the bridge hangs on)
surfaces.notes: Whole file is 85 lines: GET list (:8-22), POST upsert on (user_id, latitude, longitude) (:25-66), DELETE (:69-83). The POST validates label/lat/lng and expectedUserId (:30-37) and writes SavedPlace only — no UserNotificationPreferences row, no UserViewingLocation, no hub cache clear, exactly as F1 states. Web client mirror frontend/packages/api/src/endpoints/savedPlaces.ts has only getSavedPlaces/create/remove (:14-34).

gaps: F1 — nothing on web reads today.location.source. Grep for 'location.source' across frontend/apps/web/src returns zero hits; the only source-ish reads are display_mode (hub/today/page.tsx:177,184; HubTodayCard.tsx:112-118). The current empty branch (hub/today/page.tsx:177-181, 'No briefing available right now.') fires for BOTH a null payload and display_mode==='hidden', so it cannot tell 'no location' from 'hidden for another reason'. F1's source-aware branch needs the source value, not display_mode.

F1 — the type does not admit a saved place. HubTodayLocation.source in frontend/packages/types/src/ai.ts:302 is the closed union 'custom' | 'viewing_pinned' | 'primary_home' | 'home' | 'viewing_recent' | 'none'. Adding the resolver's 'saved_place' is a types-package change plus a rebuild of every consumer, not just a page edit.

F1 — there is no saved-place Today surface to render into. SavedPlaceContext.tsx renders only the anonymous /api/public/place preview (:29-33, :87); it has no weather, AQI, alerts, address calendar or briefing control. The design's 'Saved place · Only you' chip has two possible homes and neither is prepared: the Today tab (which shows only hub payload) or SavedPlaceContext (which never fetches hub today).

F1 — removing the last saved place will not reset Today. SavedPlaceContext's remove handler invalidates only ['place-entry', userId, 'saved'] (:72-79) and never queryKeys.hubToday(); both Today mounts hold staleTime 120_000 (hub/today/page.tsx:110, hub/page.tsx:115). The F1 acceptance 'removing the last saved place returns Today to the starts-with-a-place state' needs an explicit invalidation that does not exist.

F1 — the briefing opt-in cannot simply move. BriefingOptIn is lines 415-529 of TodayDetail.tsx (appendix cites :443-498 — stale). It lives inside a file whose only other content reads the PlaceIntelligence contract, and the component itself is fine (it only calls hub preferences), but its mount point TodayDetail is reachable only through PlaceSectionDetail, which hard-stops at 'You haven't added a place yet' when there is no primary home (PlaceSectionDetail.tsx:144-159).

F1/F4 — a pickup signal already renders wrong on the web Today tab. The backend emits kind 'address_calendar' (usefulnessEngine.js:310) but HubTodaySignal.kind (types/src/ai.ts:334) has no such member and both SignalIcon switches (hub/today/page.tsx:50-66, HubTodayCard.tsx:49-66) have a 'calendar' case and no 'address_calendar' case, so the pickup signal falls through to the default Sparkles icon today. F4's 'Today shows the same items whether or not the push fired' lands on a surface that mislabels the item.

F2 — the checklist is invisible to exactly the users F2 targets. On /app/place, PlaceDashboard returns SavedPlaceContext and stops at :133-139, before the SetupBanner mount at :157-159 — so a user with a saved place and no home never sees any checklist on the Place tab. The only other mount is /app/hub (hub/page.tsx:215), which is not a destination in the four-tab nav (MobileTabBar.tsx:22-27, AppShell.tsx:699-700). A 'save_place' step has no surface that a pre-home user can reach.

F2 — re-keying the checklist server-side will degrade silently. SetupBanner's stepConfig (SetupBanner.tsx:14-21) knows only home/verify/complete_profile/profile_photo/skills/payout_method; an unknown key renders the raw key string as its label and routes to /app/profile/edit (:45). Shipping save_place / pickup_day / important_date / household from hub.js before the client map lands would show four chips labelled 'save_place', 'pickup_day', 'important_date', 'household', all pointing at profile edit. Also /app/hub filters keys by name (hub/page.tsx:171), so renames have to be mirrored there.

F2 — the title heuristic is key-coupled. SetupBanner.tsx:34 picks 'Set up your place' only when a step keyed 'home' or 'verify' is undone; re-keying 'home' to 'save_place' silently flips the banner title to 'Complete your profile'.

F5 — no date kinds exist on web. PlaceCalendarKind (frontend/packages/types/src/placeIntelligence.ts:236-239) has the 15 shipped kinds and none of lease_end, lease_notice, insurance_renewal, warranty_end, hoa_dues, tax_appeal; KIND_ICON in AddressCalendarCard.tsx:38-54 is typed as a total Record<PlaceCalendarKind, LucideIcon>, so widening the union is a compile error until every new kind gets an icon. PlaceCalendarEvent.scope (:252) is 'home'|'city'|'county'|'state' with no 'saved_place'.

F5 — there is no 'Dates' UI of any kind. AddressCalendarCard has one control, the pickup-day picker (:166-209), and it is rendered only when homeId is truthy (:153). No kind picker, no date field, no 'Remind me' lead-days control (nothing in the web app writes lead_days at all — setPickupDay sends weekday/recycling_frequency/recycling_next_date only, :129-133), and no per-event 'You' source label (EventRow prints e.source ?? 'Pantopus registry', :86).

F5 — no saved-place calendar client and no saved-place mount point. frontend/packages/api/src/endpoints/savedPlaces.ts is list/create/remove only (:14-34); addressCalendar.ts is hard-coded to /api/homes/:id (:31-44). And AddressCalendarCard is mounted from exactly one place, TodayDetail.tsx:599, which is home-gated — so 'inside the existing address-calendar card' has no reachable instance for a T1 saved-place user. F5 on web is a new route or a new mount inside SavedPlaceContext, not an edit to the card.

F5 — the card's homeId=null path is written but dead in production. AddressCalendarCard.tsx:99-101 keys on `homeId ?? 'preview'` and :153/:166 hide the control when null, and the test exercises homeId=null (tests/addressCalendarCard.test.tsx:21), but no app code ever renders it with null. It is a half-built preview mode, not a saved-place mode: it still has no way to write anything.

F5 — the honesty copy is per-event, not per-surface. 'unconfirmed, please double-check' is appended inside EventRow (:87); there is no card-level 'Only you' / 'your household calendar' distinction, which F5's confirmation toasts assume ('Saved to your calendar. Only you.' at T1 vs 'Saved to your household calendar.' at T3). Today the only toast is 'Pickup schedule saved to your household calendar.' (:138), unconditionally.

F7 — web has nothing, and §5 attribution assumes it does. No snapshot, no widget, no deep-link handling: grep for 'src=widget', 'session_open', 't0_compare' across frontend/apps/web/src returns zero hits. F7 itself is native-only by design, but §5's return-with-attribution requires all three clients to post session_open with a trigger, and the web app has no such call site and no ?src= parsing on /app/today, /app/place, or /start.

F7 — there is no web write site for the snapshot contract either. The design names PlaceDetailViewModel.fetch() (iOS) and TodayTabViewModel.refresh() (Android) as write sites; the web equivalents (hub/today/page.tsx query at :107-112 and PlaceDashboard's intelQuery at :112-117) write nothing anywhere and would need a new mechanism if web ever mirrors it.

F11 — the named render target is effectively unreachable. Grep for 'keeper' across frontend/apps/web/src: zero hits. HubTodayCard (the F11 web target) is mounted only at app/(app)/app/hub/page.tsx:202, and /app/hub is not one of the four tabs — the reachable Today surfaces are /app/today (hub/today/page.tsx) and /app/place/today (TodayDetail.tsx). A keeper shipped into HubTodayCard would be seen only by users who click the logo.

F11 — HubTodayCard has no slot for it. The card has no kicker/avatar/header region equivalent to the iOS TodayDetailContent.kicker; its header is a location + freshness strip (:142-160) and it returns null rather than rendering an empty state when there is nothing (:112), so a keeper would vanish exactly on the quiet days its 'relaxed' mood is for.

F11 — the mood inputs are the broken hub mail counts, confirmed by reading. backend/routes/hub.js:221-227 selects Mail.id/type/is_read filtered on recipient_id + status, and :255-261 counts Mail filtered on home_id + status; both are wrapped in .catch(() => ({ count: 0 })) / ({ data: null }), so a bad column name degrades to zero with no error surfaced to any web state. Risk #9 is real and silent.

F11 — no per-home settings surface on web to hold the keeper object. Nothing in the Place area reads or writes HomePreference.settings; the only free-form preference writes on these surfaces are hub notification preferences (TodayDetail.tsx:457-461).

Cross-cutting — the saved-place surface renders in two different frames. /app/place?savedPlace= renders SavedPlaceContext bare in a 760px div with no PlaceShell and no nav rail (app/(app)/app/place/page.tsx:43-44), while the no-home fallback renders the same component inside PlaceShell active='overview' (PlaceDashboard.tsx:134-138). Any chip, Today entry or checklist F1/F2 adds to it appears in two layouts, one of which has no way back into the Place sections.

Cross-cutting — two surfaces are both called 'Today' and they gate differently. /app/today (MobileTabBar.tsx:24, AppShell.tsx:700) is the hub-payload briefing, needs no home, and re-exports hub/today/page.tsx; /app/place/today (PlaceNavRail.tsx:35) is the PlaceIntelligence detail and requires a claimed primary home. F1 changes the first; F5 and F11 target the second. The design's copy does not say which 'Today' the 'Saved place · Only you' chip belongs to, and shipping it to only one leaves the two disagreeing about whether the user has a place.

Cross-cutting — /app/place/* detail pages resolve only the PRIMARY home. PlaceSectionDetail.tsx:82-89 uses getPrimaryHome with no selectedHomeId, unlike the dashboard which honours a switcher (PlaceDashboard.tsx:44, :90). A multi-home user who switches on the dashboard and then taps into Today silently gets the primary home's calendar — relevant the moment F5 lets people write dates from that card.

Cross-cutting — no evening-briefing control exists in the Place/Today area. BriefingOptIn writes only daily_briefing_* (TodayDetail.tsx:457-461); evening_briefing_enabled / evening_briefing_time_local are settable only at app/(app)/app/settings/notifications/page.tsx:146-150. F4's night-before pickup rides the evening briefing and §5's activation definition counts evening_briefing_enabled, so the surface that would earn that opt-in has no control for it.

Cross-cutting — every error retry on the Today detail is a full page reload. TodayDetail.tsx:560, :576, :584, :592 pass onRetry={() => window.location.reload()}. Any new F5 write control on that page has to survive (or avoid) a reload-based recovery path.

Test coverage that exists and will constrain the work: frontend/apps/web/tests/savedPlaceContext.test.tsx (account-scoping, preview-refresh failure), pendingPlaceSave.test.tsx, addressCalendarCard.test.tsx (explicit-save and no-invented-recycling assertions, and a homeId=null case), justMovedCard.test.tsx (local-only storage), placeGroupDetail.test.tsx, placePulseStream.test.tsx, startFunnel.test.tsx. There is no web test for the hub Today tab's empty/loading/error branches and none for SetupBanner.

No household-verified vs address-verified distinction exists on any web surface (F3b). useHomePermissions.tsx:228 gates purely on verification_status === 'verified'; the members page role badges (members/page.tsx:16-25) and the settings "Your Role" row (settings/page.tsx:132-135) show role only; nothing displays or reads a verification source. No path from the invitation decision to address verification. F3b wants the verify sheet shown as the next step after accepting a household invite; today AuthenticatedInvitationPage's success path offers only "Check current Home access" and "Open Home" (:64-73), and VerifyPromptSheet.tsx ("What this unlocks", :153-170) is reachable only from the Place dashboard banner.

F6's server-synced ticks have no web surface to bind to. JustMovedCard state is localStorage-only (JustMovedCard.tsx:22-23, :48-59) and the card lives on the Place dashboard (PlaceDashboardView.tsx:107), not on the Home dashboard or in the homes/ area at all — so a mover who lands on /app/homes/:id/dashboard never sees the checklist. The card is invisible without Home.move_in_date. isRecentMove returns false for a null move-in date (JustMovedCard.tsx:26-27), and nothing in the homes/ area collects or edits move_in_date — /app/homes/[id]/settings exposes only nickname, address, type and role (settings/page.tsx:96-137).

Documents delete is client-only: docs/page.tsx:42-47 filters the row out of local state and toasts "Document removed" without any API call — worth knowing before F3b classifies documents as a household-verified surface members can act on.

Two parallel settings surfaces and two parallel member surfaces exist with no cross-links: /app/homes/[id]/settings vs the dashboard Settings tab (HomeSettingsTab.tsx, 636 lines), and /app/homes/[id]/members vs the dashboard Members & Security tab (MembersSecurityTab.tsx, 537 lines). F3's "Members page fix" touches only one of each pair; any copy or button change needs to be made in both or the pair needs collapsing.

gaps: The design's central Android premise is wrong: Android DOES have a saved-places client. SavedPlacesApi.kt:18-44 exposes list/save/delete against /api/saved-places, SavedPlacesRepository.kt:20-30 wraps it, SavedPlacesDtos.kt carries all four payloads, SavedPlacesScreen.kt:64-120 renders the list, and HomeTabHostViewModel.kt:73-109 already POSTs a saved place from the post-signin arrival flow. So F1 line 94 ("Android has no saved-places client"), line 107 ("Add the missing saved-places client (SavedPlacesApi …)"), §2 rule 5, the F1 effort line ("Android 2-3 days including the client") and the §6 table's 3d Android row all need correcting. The real F1 Android work is one branch in TodayTabViewModel.refresh() plus the header chip — roughly the iOS estimate, not triple it.

No Today widget, and the existing widget plumbing is not extensible as-is. One provider only (AndroidManifest.xml:126-136), one info xml (res/xml/widget_tasks_near_me_info.xml), one layout, four strings (res/values/strings.xml:16-19). WidgetSnapshotStore.kt's interface is hard-typed to List<WidgetTaskSnapshot> (L55-65), the prefs file name is "tasks_near_me_widget" (L143) and requestWidgetUpdate() broadcasts to TasksNearMeWidgetProvider::class specifically (L132). A KEY_TODAY_SNAPSHOT cannot simply be added: the interface, the prefs namespacing and the broadcast target all have to be generalized first. Confirmed no Glance dependency in app/build.gradle.kts or gradle/libs.versions.toml. Only write site is GigsFeedViewModel.kt:784, and TodayTabViewModel injects no store.

The "Scan today's stack" CTA is fully built and wired to nothing: RootTabScreen.kt:5617 passes `onScan = { /* Out of scope per A13.16 — scanner integration */ }`, and the sibling onSeeHistory / onOpenNudge at L5618-5619 are no-ops too. The CTA itself (MailboxEmptyHero.kt:171-206) and the MailDayViewModel.configure(onScanRequested=…) seam (MailDayScreen.kt:78) are ready. Mitigating: CameraX is already a dependency (app/build.gradle.kts:243-245, camerax 1.4.0 in libs.versions.toml:15) and CAMERA is already declared (AndroidManifest.xml:14), so F10's Android camera work starts from a real base.

No received-invitations list, and no client for the endpoint at all. Every Android invitation call is sender-side or token-scoped: HomeInvitationSenderApi.kt:18 is GET api/homes/{home}/invitations (invites this home sent), TokenAcceptApi.kt:37/58/65 and HomeInvitationDecisionApi.kt:14-45 are token- and decision-scoped. Backend's received list, GET /api/homes/invitations (backend/routes/home.js:1302), has zero Android callers. MyHomesListViewModel.kt loads only my-homes (L145) and residency requests (L224); MyHomesListScreen.kt:122-150 has no section to hang "Invitations waiting for you" on.

F2's checklist cannot render its copy on Android as designed. The individual step labels are never drawn: HubViewModel.kt:384-391 builds SetupStep titles mechanically from the backend key (it.key.replace('_',' ').capitalize()), so re-keying to save_place/pickup_day/important_date/household would surface as "Save place", "Pickup day", "Important date", "Household" — not the designed strings. And even those are discarded: HubScreen.kt:255-260 passes only stepsDone/stepsTotal to HubFloatingProgress, which prints "N of M steps done · K left" (HubSections.kt:1167-1169). The FirstRun state itself requires homes.isEmpty() && completeness<0.5 (HubViewModel.kt:414-417); after that only the fixed one-line amber banner remains, hard-coded to "Verify your address" / "Unlock gigs + mail receiving." (HubUiState.kt:178-181, HubSections.kt:266). Nothing renders payload.setup on the Today tab.

F5 has no seat on Android beyond pickup day. PlaceApi.kt:45-64 carries only the three home-scoped calendar routes — no saved-place calendar, no per-kind date route. The AddressCalendarActions contract (AddressCalendarActions.kt:11-18) has exactly setPickupDay/clearPickupDay, and SetPickupDayRequest is the only write model. The calendar header renders one action, "Pickup schedule" (PlaceTodayDetailContent.kt:455-463), so the "Dates" toggle, the kind picker and the lead-days chooser are all new UI plus a new interface member plus a new API surface.

F1's Today-tab branch has two structural obstacles the design does not name. First, TodayTabViewModel renders GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence (L58), never GET /api/hub/today, so there is no `today.location.source` on this screen to switch the chip on — the payload itself differs (design §3 "Two different Today payloads"). Second, the morning-briefing opt-in the design wants moved onto Today exists on Android only inside Settings -> Notifications (NotificationSettingsViewModel.kt:300-317); there is no reusable opt-in component to lift.

F3's notifications will mis-land on Android. DeepLinkRouter.kt:551-570 enumerates only residency, tasks, dashboard, members, owners, verify-landlord, verify-postcard and waiting-room under /homes/:id; everything else, including the design's bill_paid link /app/homes/:id/bills and any calendar link, falls to `else -> Destination.HomeDetail(id)` (L569) and then to homeDashboard (RootTabScreen.kt:2072-2079). The HOME_BILLS (:542) and HOME_CALENDAR (:563) routes exist but are unreachable from a push. Design rule 4 ("Every push deep-links to the exact surface") fails on Android without new parser cases.

F3's channel-parity item is stated for iOS but Android's actual hole is different. Android's invite form already offers Email and Username channels (HomeInvitationSenderContent.kt:64-83) and a post-completion share link through ACTION_SEND (L241-267); what it lacks is QR. Separately, the "Who lives here with you?" first-week card has no Android host at all — HomeDashboardScreen.kt has no members_active===1 or occupancy-age branch, and the dashboard's only member affordance is the permission-gated "Members" quick-action tile (HomeDashboardProjection.kt:129-140, HomeDashboardScreen.kt:222-227).

F6: ticks are SharedPreferences, per-home, per-device (JustMovedCard.kt:121-135, prefs "just_moved"), so nothing survives a reinstall or crosses to web/iOS. Only five steps exist (L81-118) with no `register`/voter step, and the card is gated on a move-in date via isRecentMove (L61-69) and hosted only on the Place dashboard (PlaceDashboardScreen.kt:197-212) — not on Today, and not at all when homeId is blank (L200).

F11 has no Android substrate. The `TodayDetailUiState.kicker` slot the design names (TodayDetailUiState.kt:74) belongs to the hub *briefing* screen (hub/today/…), which is a different surface from the Today *tab* (place/today/… -> PlaceTodayDetailContent.kt:58-111, which has no kicker at all). kicker is a plain String from TodayDetailMapper; there is no keeper name/species/mood model, no home-settings client writing HomePreference.settings, and no naming sheet anywhere.

§5's instrumentation has no Android emitter. There is no funnel-events API client in the Android tree — no /api/public/funnel or /api/funnel call anywhere under frontend/apps/android/app/src/main — so `session_open` (and every t0_* event F8 relies on) would need a new endpoint client, a new deep-link `?src=` parser branch (DeepLinkRouter.kt has no src handling), and a widget-snapshot-written reporter that does not exist. Activation as defined in §5 is therefore unmeasurable on Android as shipped.

Test coverage the design assumes is partly absent. F1 cites "Android TodayTabViewModel tests" — no such file exists; the only Today tests are for the hub briefing (TodayDetailViewModelTest.kt, TodayDetailMapperTest.kt, TodayDetailSnapshotTest.kt). F5's cited PickupScheduleSnapshotTest.kt exists (plus androidTest PickupScheduleEditorTest.kt) and F3's HomeInvitationSenderCoordinatorTest.kt exists. F7's model, GigsFeedViewModelTest.kt, exists and is the only place a fake WidgetSnapshotStore lives — there is no widget-provider or render-time-date test to clone.

'This invitation does not grant ownership.' sits at Features/TokenAccept/HomeInvitationDecisionView.swift:113 and a near-twin at Features/Homes/Members/InviteMemberWizardView.swift:57-59. Worse, MyHomesListViewModel already stamps a green 'Household access' chip purely off `occupancy.verificationStatus == "verified"` (:220-224) with the comment that invitation acceptance creates it without residency evidence — after F3b that chip reads as address-verified unless it is re-sourced.

The step list is hard-coded at five with no `register` voter step (:88-118), the card requires `Home.move_in_date` inside a -14…+60 day window (:22-36, :134), and its only mount is PlaceDashboardView.swift:129-135 — a saved-place user never sees it.

MailboxEmptyHero's CTA (Features/Mailbox/MailDay/Components/MailboxEmptyHero.swift:90-107) calls MailDayViewModel.requestScan() (:237), which forwards to `onScanRequested` — a closure both initializers default to `{}` (MailDayViewModel.swift:51-62, :65-75) and that both call sites leave at the default (Features/Root/YouTabRoot.swift:1019-1022, Features/Root/HubTabRoot.swift:2844-2847). The Hub's 'Scan mail' chip is a second dead end: declared `active: false` (Features/Hub/HubViewModel.swift:439) and routed to the mailbox root (HubTabRoot.swift:1058).

F10 — no client for creating a Mail Day item, with or without an image. MailDayEndpoints has only today / route / finish (Core/Networking/Endpoints/MailDayEndpoints.swift:14-28); there is no POST …/mailday/items, no multipart helper, and no editable extracted-field UI. The camera plumbing exists and is reusable (Core/Design/Components/SystemCameraPicker.swift:13, wired in Features/Mailbox/Unboxing/UnboxingView.swift:110), so the gap is the API client plus a confirm step, not the capture.

F11 — the keeper has no storage client and its named render slot is on the wrong screen. No iOS code reads or writes HomePreference.settings (the per-home settings screen is navigation-only: Features/Homes/Settings/HomeSettingsViewModel.swift:5-8, :18-21). The `kicker` slot F11 names exists on TodayDetailContent (Features/Hub/Today/TodayDetailContent.swift:147, set at TodayDetailViewModel.swift:190) but that view only mounts behind a briefing push (RootTabView.swift:257-263) — the actual Today tab renders PlaceTodayDetailContent, which has no kicker slot, so the keeper needs a second render site.

Cross-cutting — Today exists twice on iOS with different payloads and different states. The tab renders the Place intelligence payload (GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence, per-section ready/stale/partial fallbacks, PlaceTodayDetailContent.swift:27-87) while the briefing screen renders GET /api/hub/today (TodayDetailViewModel.swift:124) with loading/populated/alert/error and no empty state. Any F1/F5/F11 copy has to be written twice or the two screens have to be reconciled first; the design's iOS notes only address the tab.

Cross-cutting — test coverage is thin exactly where the design lands. There are no PantopusTests for AddressTodayTabView or PlaceTodayDetailContent (PantopusTests/Features/Place holds decoding and presentation tests only); the widget snapshot has one test site (PantopusTests/Features/Gigs/GigsFeedViewModelTests.swift); the useful existing anchors are PantopusTests/AddressCalendarContractTests.swift, PantopusTests/JustMovedCardTests.swift, PantopusTests/Features/Homes/Members/InviteMemberWizardViewModelTests.swift and PantopusTests/Features/Hub/TodayDetailViewModelTests.swift.

screens.hostSurface: OS home screen. iOS: new frontend/apps/ios/PantopusWidgets/TodayWidget.swift, registered as a third entry in frontend/apps/ios/PantopusWidgets/PantopusWidgetsBundle.swift:14-17, with frontend/apps/ios/Pantopus/Core/Widgets/TodayWidgetSnapshot.swift added to PantopusWidgets.sources in frontend/apps/ios/project.yml:229-235. Android: new frontend/apps/android/app/src/main/java/app/pantopus/android/widget/TodayWidgetProvider.kt cloned from TasksNearMeWidgetProvider.kt:36-159, plus res/layout/widget_today.xml, res/xml/widget_today_info.xml and a sibling <receiver> in AndroidManifest.xml next to the one at :126-136. Data comes from the snapshot only — the extension can never call the API (keychain is app-private, AUTH_DEVICE_BINDING=required).
screens.purpose: Give the address a reason to be on the home screen: the three true facts about today — pickup, air, next date — visible without opening the app and without a push.
screens.contents: Place label line + three data lines, any of which can be nil. Densest realistic content: place label '1402 NE 3rd Ave'; line 1 pickup 'Recycling + garbage Tue' with an ·unconfirmed glyph; line 2 air 'AQI 42 Good' with a tone dot; line 3 next date 'Lease notice · 12d'. A greyed 'Open to refresh' footer replaces nothing but tints the whole stack past 6h. Relative day words ('today'/'tomorrow'/'in 12 days') are computed at render time from the stored ISO date, never from a stored days_until — so the widest string must always fit. Snapshot contract per the doc: TodayWidgetSnapshot { generatedAt, placeLabel, nextPickup{kind,date,unverified}?, aqi{index,label}?, nextDate{kind,title,date}? }, key todaySnapshotV1, kind TodayWidget, same App Group group.app.pantopus.ios / KEY_TODAY_SNAPSHOT. DESIGNER: decide the vertical rhythm for a 4x2 cell that must hold four text rows legibly at the smallest supported dynamic type AND survive all three lines being present with the longest strings ('Recycling + garbage Tue ·unconfirmed', 'AQI 151 Unhealthy for sensitive groups', 'Property tax due · in 12 days') — and pick which single line gets promoted when one is urgent.
entryPoints: OS widget picker: long-press home screen → add widget → Pantopus → 'Today at your address' (see f7-widget-gallery-entry)
Tap anywhere on the widget → pantopus://today?src=widget (iOS widgetURL; Android PendingIntent on the root RemoteViews)
NO in-app discovery path exists today — f7-add-widget-nudge is the only one, and without it this widget is only findable by someone already hunting the OS widget gallery

screens.uxRisk: Four real risks. (1) THE STALE TRAP: 'Open to refresh' can open the app and refresh nothing — iOS PlaceDetailViewModel.load() is idempotent once .loaded (:34-37) and Android TodayTabViewModel.load() is idempotent once Loaded, so a warm app re-entered from the widget writes no new snapshot and the widget stays grey forever. The ?src=widget landing MUST call refresh(), not load(). (2) WHICH ADDRESS: StaticConfiguration + one snapshot key means a user with two homes plus a saved place gets a widget silently mirroring whichever Today resolved last; placeLabel is the only tell, so it must never be the line that truncates. Pilot scale (one address per mover) makes StaticConfiguration acceptable, but the moment multi-home matters this needs AppIntentConfiguration on iOS and an appWidgetId-keyed snapshot on Android. (3) THREE EQUAL LINES READ AS A LIST OF NOTHING — the doc's flat three-line stack gives a lease notice 12 days out the same weight as tomorrow's recycling. Better: promote the one line whose date is ≤1 day away or whose AQI ≥101 into a large hero line and demote the other two to a single secondary row; the widget then says one thing loudly instead of three things quietly. (4) 'Set your pickup day' is a to-do in a surface the user added to feel informed; make it the demoted line, never the hero.

The promotion rule is the design: urgency = nextPickup.date within 1 day > aqi.index ≥ 101 > nextDate.date nearest > nextPickup any > aqi any. DESIGNER: draw the promotion ladder, not a shrunken medium — show the same snapshot rendering as four different small widgets depending on which fact won, and prove each fits at the largest accessibility text size.

Second risk: the doc never says what small drops, so without an explicit promotion ladder each platform will invent its own and the two will disagree. Cloning that for Today means a brand-new user browsing the gallery is sold the widget with the words 'Save an address to see today here'. Same on iOS: placeholder(in:) must return a populated sample snapshot, not nil, or the gallery advertises the placeholder.

loaded, refresh failed (keep last content, inline 'Couldn't refresh' — never blank a screen the user tapped a widget to reach)

screens.uxRisk: CONFIRMED ANDROID BUG, not a risk: DeepLinkRouter.kt:494-503 maps 'today' → Destination.HubToday, and RootTabScreen.kt:2226-2233 sends that to todayDetail(deliveryId, kind) — the hub BRIEFING screen backed by GET /api/hub/today. So an Android widget tap lands on a different payload than the widget showed, and for a T1 saved-place user (pre-F1, where resolveLocation never reads SavedPlace) that screen has no empty state and hard-errors with "Today's briefing isn't available". iOS only avoids this by accident: TodayTabRoot renders TodayDetailView solely when a push supplied a deliveryId (RootTabView.swift:257-263) and otherwise falls to AddressTodayTabView. Fix: route ?src=widget explicitly to root/today on Android. Second confirmed gap: iOS parses the URL but discards src, and NO funnel-event client exists on either native platform (no recordFunnelEvent / funnel-events call anywhere under frontend/apps/ios/Pantopus or frontend/apps/android/app/src/main) — so §5's activation rule ('a widget snapshot written, reported by the client as an event') and its return-with-attribution have no emitter at all. That client is F7 work, not F8 work, because the widget is the only trigger F7 can prove. Third: the idempotent-load stale trap described on the medium widget is fixed here or nowhere.

screens.name: "Put today on your home screen" row
screens.hostSurface: The Today tab (SCREEN 2, the intelligence one) — iOS frontend/apps/ios/Pantopus/Features/Place/Detail/AddressTodayTabView.swift loaded body, below PlaceTodayDetailContent; Android frontend/apps/android/.../ui/screens/place/today/TodayTabScreen.kt:46-72 Loaded branch, inside the existing verticalScroll. Deliberately NOT the hub briefing screen — the widget mirrors this payload.
screens.purpose: Give the widget an in-app entry point. Today it has none, yet §5 counts a written widget snapshot as an activation signal equal to the briefing — a surface nobody can find cannot activate anyone.
screens.contents: One row: glyph + 'Put today on your home screen' + subline 'Pickup, air and your next date. No notifications needed.' + chevron, with a dismiss affordance. Suppressed automatically once a widget is placed (iOS WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations, Android AppWidgetManager.getAppWidgetIds for TodayWidgetProvider) and while the user has no place. DESIGNER: one row, below the real content, that reads as an offer rather than an ad — and a thumbnail of the user's own widget rendered from their live snapshot is the strongest version of it.

no place — hidden (there is nothing for the widget to show yet)
notifications denied — this row is the BETTER offer and should rank above the briefing opt-in, not below it
screens.uxRisk: Two ways to get this wrong. (1) A permanent, undismissable promo inside the one screen we want people to trust: it must self-suppress on placement detection and stay below the day's actual content. (2) Making it a first-open modal — that trains dismissal and steals the moment the user came for. The row is also the honest answer to a user who declined push notifications, since the widget is the only return trigger that needs no permission at all; ranking it above the briefing opt-in for that user is the best UX in the whole feature.

screens.name: Add-the-widget how-to sheet
screens.hostSurface: Presented from f7-add-widget-nudge — iOS a .sheet with medium detent over AddressTodayTabView; Android a ModalBottomSheet over TodayTabScreen.
screens.purpose: No public API on either platform can place a widget for the user, so the only way this converts is by teaching the three OS gestures — with a preview of their own widget so the reward is visible before the work.
screens.contents: A live preview of the user's own Today widget rendered from their real snapshot ('this is what yours will look like'), then three numbered steps with platform-correct wording — iOS: touch and hold the home screen → tap + → search Pantopus → pick a size → Add Widget; Android: touch and hold the home screen → Widgets → Pantopus → drag Today onto a screen. A 'Done' dismiss; no fake 'Add it for me' button. DESIGNER: the densest element is the live widget preview at true size above three compact illustrated steps — the sheet must fit a medium detent without scrolling on a small phone, and the step art differs per OS so it is two drawings, not one.
entryPoints: The Settings → Notifications → Briefings 'Home screen widget' row, so a user who dismissed the nudge can still get here — WITHOUT that second entry point this sheet is unreachable after one dismissal, which is a bug
states: default (live preview from the user's snapshot)
no snapshot yet — preview falls back to the representative sample used in the gallery
no place — should not be reachable; if reached, the sheet's CTA becomes 'Save an address first'
iOS copy variant vs Android copy variant (two distinct step sets)
screens.uxRisk: Instruction sheets are usually skipped. The mitigation is that the preview, not the instructions, is the top of the sheet — the user sees their own recycling day and AQI before being asked to do anything. Risk of going stale: OS gesture wording drifts between iOS and Android versions, so keep the steps to gestures ('touch and hold the home screen') rather than naming exact menu items where possible, and never screenshot a specific OS version.

ae599a6db8e2c2e4f.reasoning:
Six surfaces, none on web. F7 is native-only by design and I did not invent a web entry: the web app has no home screen to put a widget on, and the one web-adjacent hole (no ?src= parsing and no session_open call site anywhere in frontend/apps/web/src) belongs to §5/F8's attribution work, not to F7. Worth saying plainly so the parent agent does not expect a web row.

Why more than the doc's two widgets. The doc names exactly two deliverables (a small and medium widget per platform) and then quietly assumes four more surfaces exist. Rule 4 says a surface with no entry point is a bug, and as written the widget has no entry point at all: nothing in either app mentions it, so the only discovery path is a user spontaneously browsing the OS widget gallery. That forces two of my entries (the nudge row and the how-to sheet) and makes a third — the gallery entry itself — a real designed artifact rather than two strings. §5 makes this load-bearing rather than nice-to-have: activation counts "a widget snapshot written, reported by the client as an event" as equal to the briefing toggle, so an undiscoverable widget silently costs a third of the activation definition. The nudge is also the only return trigger that survives a user declining push permission, which is why I argue it should outrank the briefing opt-in for that user.

Why small and medium are two entries and not one. They are two different compositions, not one scaled: the medium holds four text rows, the small holds one promoted fact plus a chip. The doc says "small and medium" and never says what small drops, which is exactly the kind of decision that will otherwise be made twice, differently, by iOS and Android. I gave the small an explicit urgency promotion ladder. I did the same to the medium as a uxRisk: three equal-weight lines give tomorrow's recycling the same emphasis as a lease notice twelve days out, so the better design promotes one hero line and demotes the rest.

Why the tap landing is its own entry. It is the feature's only interactive moment and it is currently broken on Android: DeepLinkRouter.kt:494-503 sends "today" to Destination.HubToday, which RootTabScreen.kt:2226-2233 resolves to the hub briefing screen (GET /api/hub/today) — a different payload from the one the widget mirrors (GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence), and one with no empty state, so a T1 saved-place user gets a hard error from tapping their own widget. iOS avoids it only by accident. The same entry carries the second must-fix: both Today view models are idempotent once loaded (iOS PlaceDetailViewModel.load() :34-37, Android TodayTabViewModel.load()), so "Open to refresh" can open a warm app, write no snapshot, and leave the widget grey permanently — the landing has to call refresh(), not load(). And neither native app has any funnel-event client at all, so the emitter §5 depends on is F7 scope, not F8 scope.

What I deliberately folded rather than listed. (a) The Settings → Notifications → Briefings re-entry row is one row, so it lives inside the how-to sheet's entry points rather than as a seventh entry — but it is required, not optional: without it, one dismissal of the nudge makes the sheet permanently unreachable. (b) The placeholder, stale, unverified-pickup and no-place renderings are states of the widget entries, not separate surfaces, even though each is a distinct drawing — they are listed exhaustively per widget so the design pack still gets them. (c) I did not invent a widget configuration screen: StaticConfiguration is right for a 30-mover pilot where each user has one address, and I recorded the multi-home ambiguity as a uxRisk on the medium instead. (d) I did not add a settings toggle, because F7 introduces no persisted preference — the widget's on/off switch is the OS home screen itself.

Effort adds to roughly 6.75 days per platform against the doc's 6, the difference being the discovery surfaces the doc omitted.

Five surfaces, and only one of them is genuinely new. F6 is described as a migration plus a sixth row, and most of it really is an extension: the Just Moved card exists on all three platforms and only changes its storage, its step count and its states, so that is one entry with three platforms rather than three entries.

What I added beyond the doc, and why. (1) The voter step sheet. The doc routes the step to /app/place/civic, but I verified that Civic detail renders districts, a ballot preview and 'No upcoming election' and has no registration content, and that PlaceSectionDetail requires a claimed primary home — so the doc's own step copy (deadline, three method dates, state office, self-report, 'never claim to know whether the user is registered') has nowhere to live. A sheet keeps the fact next to the tap and is where the honesty labeling and the 'I did this' receipt belong. (2) The Civic registration block, because the card hides 60 days after move-in while the November 3 deadline does not — without it the feature deletes itself before it matters. (3) The move-in date row, because it is the gate for everything: web can edit it (/app/homes/[id]/edit:320) but both natives can only stamp today from an add-home checkbox and have no correction path, so on iOS and Android the acceptance criteria are literally unreachable today. (4) The calendar/Today rendering entry, because seeded state-scoped election_deadline rows will surface through composeForHome into the address-calendar card and, inside the lead window, as an address_calendar signal on the hub Today — whether or not anyone designs for it. F6 does not mention this and it is the most likely place for the 'read as a claim about this address' failure.

What I deliberately folded rather than counted. The dismiss confirmation and undo are states of the card, not a screen; the restore control is a second row on the settings screen I was already extending, so those two share one entry. The 'all six done' celebration, the offline queued-tick chip and the self-report receipt are card states. The 'Just moved in? Tell us when' prompt is a state of the card's currently-empty slot, not a new surface, though it writes the same field as the settings row.

What I did not invent. No push, so no new notification landing target: F6 proposes no reminder, and the generic reminder channel would need an explicit lead_days decision before a deep-link target is worth drawing. No T1 saved-place variant of the checklist: HomeOccupancy is per-user-per-home, so the checklist cannot exist for a saved place at all — that is F2's job, and the two lists must not read as the same thing. No admin surface for seed verification; the state-deadline checking is internal work.

One structural gap to flag rather than design around: every surface here is home-gated, so the mover F1 is designed to win — someone who saved a place and has not claimed a home — sees none of it. And the three Today references are deliberate: the card and the sheet live on the Place dashboard (neither Today), the calendar row lands on Today screen 2 (intelligence), and the same row leaks to Today screen 1 (hub) as a signal.

Effort excludes backend: the doc's migration + route is 1 day and the seed verification 1-2 days, on top of the per-platform days above. The sheet's read path (a rule further out than composeForHome's 14 days) is an unlisted backend line item.

a53840938374efaba.reasoning:
Eight entries, seven of which are extensions or cards inside screens that already exist — F5 genuinely needs no new route on any platform, and I resisted adding one. What I did add against the doc is the Your dates card (f5-your-dates-card), and it is not optional: composeForHome (backend/services/addressCalendarService.js:108-166) expands rules only inside windowDays=14, so under the doc's design as written a user saves a lease end eight months out, gets a toast, and the date is then invisible and undeletable in the product until two weeks before it fires. The doc's chosen host — a 14-day window card — structurally cannot be the management surface for annual dates, so its own acceptance criterion ('sees both on Today') is false for almost every date the feature exists to capture. That card is a NEW_CARD_IN_EXISTING rather than a route because the schema caps the list at one row per kind: at most six dates plus pickup, which is a card, not a screen.

I folded rather than split in four places. The pickup-day picker does not get its own entry — making the existing card scope-aware (home | saved_place) is the same change that unblocks pickup at T1, and the doc's separate 'Pickup schedule' toggle should arguably collapse into the date sheet as a seventh kind. The 'Remind me' lead-days control is part of the sheet, not a settings surface. The confirmation toasts are copy inside the sheet. The permission-denied experience for a household member without calendar.edit is a state on three entries rather than a screen — though it exposes a real hole: neither web TodayDetail nor the native Today view models read the home permission model at all, so the intelligence payload has to carry can_edit or the gate cannot be drawn.

I kept f5-t1-calendar-host separate from the card extension even though it renders the same components, because it is different work on a different screen against a different payload. Today exists twice on every platform: F5's card lives on the PlaceIntelligence Today (web /app/place/today, iOS AddressTodayTabView, Android TodayTabScreen) which requires a claimed primary home, while the T1 user's only reachable Today is the hub-payload Today (web /app/today), which carries no address_calendar section at all — pickup reaches it only as a signals[] entry whose kind is not even in the web type union. So on web the T1 card is a second query on that page, not a new field in the hub payload. Without this entry, T1 dates exist in the database and appear on no screen the user can reach.

f5-reminder-landing and f5-household-calendar-dates are entry-point and honesty obligations rather than new product surface. The reminder push has no working target today on any platform: web notificationRoutes.ts has no case, iOS and Android routers parse only deliveryId/kind, and Android sends every unrecognised /homes/:id child to the home dashboard — a push that lands on the wrong screen is the failure mode design rule 4 exists to prevent. The household calendar merge exists because the T3 toast promises 'your household calendar' and that calendar does not contain AddressCalendarRule rows; it also picks up a free win, since the fully built web household calendar at /app/homes/[id]/calendar currently has no link from anywhere in the app.

On effort: these sum to roughly 5-6 days per platform against the doc's budget of web 1.5 / iOS 2 / Android 2. The gap is almost entirely the management list, the T1 host and the deep-link landing — the three things the doc's effort line assumes are free because it assumed the card it names is reachable at T1 and can display an annual date. It is not, and it cannot.

a1578bfcbb87528c4.reasoning:
Eight surfaces: four for F11, four for F12. The doc names three render targets for F11 and claims F12 needs "no code changes beyond the kind" — both understate the real surface count, and both are wrong in ways the verified map proves.

WHICH TODAY, explicitly. F11's keeper strip lands on the Today each platform actually shows: web /app/today (= hub/today/page.tsx, SCREEN 1, GET /api/hub/today), iOS AddressTodayTabView and Android TodayTabScreen (SCREEN 2, GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence). The doc's named targets — HubTodayCard (mounted only at /app/hub, not a tab) and the iOS/Android `kicker` (the push-only briefing screen) — would put the keeper where almost nobody goes, so the briefing kicker becomes a second, thin entry (natives only; on web both Todays are the same file) rather than the primary home. F12's calendar and radon work all lands on SCREEN 2 and on the risk section detail. A third payload complication the doc does not flag: mood is computed in GET /api/hub, which neither Today screen fetches, so the keeper block has to be emitted on both Today payloads or the strip has nothing to render.

WHAT I FOLDED IN RATHER THAN COUNTING SEPARATELY. Rename / change species / remove keeper go into the fact-ledger sheet's overflow instead of a new settings screen, so one surface serves T1 (UserNotificationPreferences.settings) and T3 (HomePreference.settings) identically — and because no platform has a per-home settings surface that reads or writes HomePreference.settings today, a "Keeper" row on the existing settings index is listed as an entry point, not a screen. The "This isn't right" report is a control inside the event detail sheet, not a flow — it needs a backend endpoint that does not exist, flagged there. The 24-state avatar set (6 species x 4 moods) is a design deliverable noted on the strip, not a surface. No keeper widget line and no keeper push: the doc's honesty rule says it never nags to open the app, and F7's three widget lines are spoken for.

WHAT I ADDED THAT THE DOC IMPLIES BUT DOES NOT NAME. The fact ledger: "Ollie knows 6 things about this place" is a dead number unless the six are visible and the gaps are tappable — this is the surface that makes the keeper a retention mechanism instead of decoration, and it is the durable form of the F2 checklist, which today has no real host on any platform. The calendar event detail sheet: F12 ships unchecked county deadlines with jargon titles, and without a sheet that explains, sources, reminds and lets people dispute, F12 is a machine for producing exactly the "that's not my deadline" reports §5 counts. Both are outside the doc's effort table (F11 3d/platform, F12 "code hours"); realistically F11 is ~4.5 days per platform with the ledger, and F12 ~2.5 per platform with the sheet and provenance work.

ENTRY-POINT AND DEPENDENCY BUGS TO FLAG. The tax-appeal reminder push has no working target on Android — DeepLinkRouter.kt:551-570 falls through to the home dashboard for anything outside its eight enumerated children, so /place/today?event= must be added. The T1 keeper has no host at all until F1 ships a saved-place Today: today there is no saved-place Today surface on any platform. And the keeper's mood cannot ship before risk #9 is fixed — hub.js:221-260 swallows invalid-column errors to zero, so a broken query renders as a cheerful "relaxed" on the day a bill is overdue, which is a lie on the one metric the pilot scores at zero.

abadec2342465183a.reasoning:
F4 is written in the doc as a backend-only feature ('no client work beyond copy'), and that is the single biggest error in it. Three of the seven surfaces below are load-bearing client work the doc never names: nobody can turn the evening briefing on without three taps in Settings (f4-4), the gate's most common outcome — silence — renders as an error on Android and as a conflated empty branch on web (f4-3), and the in-app equivalent the design's own rule 4 promises does not exist on the screen most users open (f4-7).

I deliberately made the two Todays explicit on every entry. The push and its landing card (f4-1, f4-2), the quiet-day state (f4-3) and the alert variant (f4-8) all live on Today #1, GET /api/hub/today — web /app/today, iOS TodayDetailView, Android hub/today. The confirm-or-correct editor (f4-6) and the tonight row (f4-7) live on Today #2, GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence — web /app/place/today, iOS AddressTodayTabView, Android TodayTabScreen. The opt-in card (f4-4) has to sit on whichever Today the platform actually lands users on, which is #1 on web and #2 on both natives; that split is the main reason it is one entry with three different host files.

Two entry-point bugs, flagged rather than designed around: on iOS and Android, Today #1 is reachable only by tapping a briefing push, so the pickup card and the quiet-day state are invisible to anyone with notifications off — the exact population rule 4 exists for; and the pickup editor renders only when homeId is non-null, so the push's own caveat CTA ('Set your pickup day to make it yours') dead-ends for the T1 saved-place users F1 creates, until F5 ships the saved_place calendar scope. F4 should not push an unverified pickup to anyone who has no way to confirm it.

Where the doc is clumsy I said so rather than drawing it: the confirm path is buried in a card-header toggle on a scrolled page, which is a poor destination for a tray tap — f4-6 proposes a sheet that opens pre-filled with the guessed day and returns the user where they were. And I turned the §5 honesty counter's 'user report tagged not my schedule' into an actual affordance — the confirm/correct pair on f4-2 and f4-7 — because the doc assumes that report exists with no surface to file it from.

Folded in rather than listed separately: the OS notification-permission-denied case is a state on f4-4 and f4-5, not its own screen; the 'why didn't I get one' explanation is the receipt line in f4-3 plus the caption in f4-5; the per-signal icon and the address_calendar type-union hole are contents of f4-2 rather than a separate surface. Deliberately not invented: a briefings history/list screen (the design's in-app equivalent is Today, and a dismissed push is recoverable through the tonight row), a separate pickup-reminder preference (the evening briefing preference is the channel), and any web push surface — web genuinely gets no night-before push, which is why f4-7 carries the whole feature there and is the cheapest entry in the list.

a4ee2364cb2fc1adf.feature: F1 Save sets location (the bridge) + F2 three-question first week checklist — docs/first-person-loop-design-2026-09-16.md:88-140
a4ee2364cb2fc1adf.reasoning:
Ten surfaces, no new routes and no new widget. F1 and F2 are both "make an existing screen finally work for a T1 saved-place user," so almost everything is a branch, a chip, a card or a sheet on surfaces that already ship. I deliberately kept it to ten by folding several candidates in: the OS-notification permission primer is a STATE of the briefing opt-in card, not its own screen; the checklist's "household" row lands on the existing Add Home / invite flows, so it needs no new destination; a checklist detail screen is unjustified at 3-5 rows; and the briefing push already has a working home-free landing target (pantopus://hub-today?deliveryId= renders the hub payload on both natives), so F1 adds no push target. I explicitly did NOT treat web /app/hub as a host — it is not one of the four tabs, so anything mounted only there is invisible by construction (this is why F2 cannot be solved by re-keying SetupBanner).

Three surfaces the doc does not name but strictly needs. (1) The "Where Today gets this" sheet — F1 puts a "Saved place · Only you" chip on Today, but the resolver silently picks the NEWEST SavedPlace, so a user with several saved places cannot tell why Today shows one of them or change it. Without the sheet the chip is a dead label and the precedence rule is unexplainable. (2) The remove-saved-place confirmation — F1's own acceptance criterion is "removing the last saved place returns Today to the starts-with-a-place state," which is a destructive action with an invisible consequence, made worse by web's remove handler never invalidating queryKeys.hubToday against two mounts holding staleTime 120s. (3) The pickup-day quick-set sheet — F2's second checklist row has NO destination at any tier until F5 ships the saved-place calendar routes, and the build order puts F2 before F5. A checklist row that opens nothing is exactly the entry-point bug to flag; either that sheet moves ahead of F2 or the checklist hides rows whose destination does not exist yet.

On which Today each surface lands: every F1 surface and the F2 card land on Screen 1, the GET /api/hub/today payload (web /app/today -> hub/today/page.tsx, iOS TodayDetailView, Android hub/today content). None of them touch Screen 2 (GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence) — that is F5's and F11's territory. The structural cost is on the natives: their Today TAB currently renders Screen 2 and requires a home id, so F1 makes one tab render two different payloads with different sections and different failure modes. iOS at least already owns a Screen-1 renderer (TodayDetailView, today reachable only from a briefing push); Android's Today tab has no Screen-1 renderer at all and must embed the hub TodayDetail content, which is why its bridge cost is 3x web's.

Two corrections to the doc that change scope: Android already has a full saved-places client (SavedPlacesApi/Repository/Screen, and HomeTabHostViewModel already POSTs one), so F1's Android cost is the Today-tab payload branch, not a new client; and the briefing opt-in is NOT a "move" on the natives — no briefing control exists anywhere outside Settings > Notifications on iOS or Android, so that card is net-new twice. Adding the management, confirm, source-sheet and native-card work, this inventory totals roughly 7 web days, 7.5 iOS days and 9.5 Android days against the doc's budget of 1.5 / 2.5 / 4 for F1+F2 combined.

Entry-point bugs found: the web saved-places surface (SavedPlaceContext at /app/place?savedPlace=all) has no nav entry anywhere and renders frameless in a bare 760px div, so a web user who saves a place can never find it again — that must be fixed before F1 hangs a "Used for Today" badge on it; and the F2 pickup row noted above.

The fix is a contract change, not a re-key: the backend must ship label, body, route and tier-gate per step and every client renders from the payload. a5f5395f832db7d82.feature: F3 Household is the first network + F3b address-verified vs household-verified
a5f5395f832db7d82.reasoning:
F3 reads like four items (permissions migration, first-week card, received-invite list, three notifications) plus a copy change for F3b. In the real codebase it is fifteen user-visible surfaces, because the migration silently turns on screens that were never designed for a non-manager and because three of the named surfaces are currently lies or orphans.

What I merged rather than counted twice: the F3b "household member" chip lives on the members roster, so it is inside the members entry, not its own; the Members "Invite" button fix is the same screen as the roster, so it is inside that entry too; the "Verify the address yourself" next step after accepting and the "you need address verification to do this" block are ONE sheet with two entry points, not two sheets; the bill_paid deep-link landing is the bills screen, so it is inside the bills entry; "Just me" is a state of the first-week card (with an undo toast), not a confirmation screen; QR/link parity is a channel inside the existing invite wizard.

What I added that the doc does not name but needs. (a) A pending-invite entry on the landing surface: the doc puts received invites only on My Homes, but an invited co-resident typically has no home at all, never opens My Homes, and on native the app auto-lands on the Place dashboard — without this the invite is reachable only by re-finding the original email. (b) The address-verification-required state on the eight attested surfaces: F3b flips isVerifiedResident to false for household members, and today that means controls silently vanish or return a raw 403 — a household member who taps "Get a residency letter" must be told why, not shown nothing. (c) An entry point for the web household calendar, which is fully built (HomeAgenda with a gated read-only mode) and has zero links anywhere — F3's acceptance criterion "an invited member can read and edit the calendar" cannot pass on web without it; it is the cheapest win in the feature. (d) A notification-preferences surface: three new co-resident notification types ship with no honest off switch anywhere, and the per-home toggles that look like one are local useState with a "real impl would persist" comment. (e) The INVITE_POLICY_CHANGED reissue state on both the recipient and sender side — the doc's own acceptance criterion requires the recipient message, but without a sender-side "Needs reissue" row the recipient is told to ask someone who can see nothing. (f) The member read-only rendering of the home dashboard and bills: the migration hands members finance.view without finance.manage, so every manage action on those cards has to have a designed absent-with-reason state or the dashboard reads as broken.

Honesty flags carried into the entries: the web Members "Invite" button routes to an add-guest page that makes no API call and toasts success unconditionally — F3 demotes it to "secondary", which means shipping a lying screen on purpose unless it is wired or disabled; iOS already stamps a green "Household access" chip off verification_status === 'verified', which directly contradicts F3b and must be re-labeled in the same PR; Android's DeepLinkRouter enumerates only 8 /homes/:id children, so the bill_paid and home_event_created links land on the dashboard instead of the bill or the event; the web bill delete writes 'cancelled' while the filter excludes 'canceled'.

Effort: I priced per platform for one platform and deliberately came out above the doc's F3 line (web 2d / iOS 3d / Android 2d, plus F3b 1–2d). The doc's number covers the card, the list, the copy and the iOS channels. It does not cover the read-only variants the permission migration creates, the attested-action gating states, the notification routing, or the reissue path — roughly 5–6 more days per platform, and web carries an extra penalty because members and settings each exist twice (standalone route + dashboard tab) with no cross-links, so every copy or button change has to be made in both or the pair drifts. The iOS home dashboard (Features/Homes/HomeDashboardView.swift, HomeDashboardProjection.swift) was not enumerated in the verified map; I confirmed by reading that it gates cards and quick actions on members.view / finance.view / calendar.view and already carries membersActive, so the first-week card and the read-only variants have a real host there.

a8d1ec906762264cb.reasoning:
Nine surfaces, from a feature the doc describes in one dense paragraph of client work ("wire the existing CTAs to the camera, show extracted fields as editable chips, add a web Mail Day page"). The count comes from following the object the user creates all the way through: a photograph becomes an upload, an extraction, a mail piece, a bill, a calendar row, a reminder, and a file that must be deletable — each of those is somewhere the user has to look.

Only two things here are genuinely new full screens, and only on one platform: the web Mail Day triage page (web has no triage surface at all today — /app/mailbox/settings/mail-day is settings plus a read-only summary, and the only wired Mail Day clients are p3/mailday/summary and /settings). Everywhere else I stayed at sheet, card or extend, because the triage screen, the bills surfaces, the address-calendar card, the mailbox drawers and the notification lists all already exist on three platforms. I kept the per-platform disposition split explicit in the contents of f10-1 rather than inventing two entries, since it is one conceptual screen with a 2-day web cost and a 0.75-day native cost.

Surfaces the doc implies but never names, which I added: the photo viewer (f10-4) — the doc promises private, authenticated, deletable storage and then gives the photograph no place to be seen or removed, which would make it write-only; the privacy/storage card (f10-8) — the same promise needs a bulk exit, not per-bill deletion; the push landing (f10-7) — §2 rule 4 demands every push deep-link to the exact surface, and today Android's router has no /homes/:id/bills branch at all and web has no bill detail route, so the monthly-return loop breaks silently; and the photographed mail piece in the drawers (f10-9), which is where the record actually lives after triage ends.

Folded rather than split: the "Scan today's stack" CTA wiring (a state/entry point of f10-1 and f10-2, not a screen); the T1 no-claimed-home tier gate (a state on f10-1, f10-2, f10-3 and f10-6, routed to F5's manual dates — F10 explicitly requires a claimed home in v1); the AI-unavailable manual path (a state of f10-3, not a second sheet); mark-paid confirmation and undo (states on f10-5 and f10-6, since Mark paid already ships on all three platforms); and the web bill delete 'cancelled'/'canceled' bug, which is a one-line fix inside f10-5 but reproduces a visible lie on the newest path.

Two places I pushed back on the doc. The "editable chips" confirmation is the wrong control for a currency, a date and a payee, and it hides which field the model was unsure about — I propose photo-beside-fields with per-field confidence and keep chips only for the collapsed row summary. And treating the camera as a one-shot picker fights the actual task, which is a stack of mail on one evening — the capture tray should be a batch session with a thumbnail strip, and the snap affordance should be persistent rather than living only in the empty state, where both natives currently put it.

Effort lands near the doc's web 4d / iOS 5d / Android 5d, with web slightly over because the doc's estimate assumes a Mail Day page that does not exist and a Mail Day client that is only half-wired.

ae88d841c546542a8.reasoning:
F9 is seven backend/copy items, so the honest answer is mostly EXTEND_EXISTING and COPY_ONLY. But four of the seven have no user-visible surface today, and shipping them blind would either be invisible (coordinate leak) or read as a bug (Earn 404s), so I surfaced the rows and states they imply rather than inventing screens.

What I deliberately did NOT create: no screen for the seeder-prompt item — humanizer.py's ENGAGEMENT and sports lines are generator-side, and its only user-visible consequences are that curator posts read less human (covered by the curator chip) and that curator rows stop inflating organic counts (folded into the cells-map entry rather than inventing a "counts" screen). No new screen for the coordinate-leak fix itself — one row in the existing privacy mirror is its whole user-facing footprint. No new founding screens; the rank/tier rename is copy on surfaces that already exist.

Where I split rather than merged: (a) the invite-rewards card is one concept but genuinely NEW on web (frontend/packages/api/src/endpoints/users.ts:210 has zero callers; web has no referral UI at all) versus EXTEND on iOS/Android, with different effort — so it is two entries carrying the disposition each platform actually gets; (b) the two founding-naming passes are separate because the Block detail needs a real visual decision (rank badge vs tier pill, currently one paragraph) while the verify promise lists are pure string edits.

Where I went beyond the doc, and why: the curator explainer sheet (the doc's own "keep report/mute available" assumes the reader knows what a curator post is — "curator" is internal vocabulary) and the Earn landing state (the doc says 404; a 404 on a route the app linked last week is a trust bug, and a user with a pending payout must never be locked out of their money).

Entry-point bugs found, all real: unlocked referral tiers have no destination on any platform — an unlocked reward the user cannot navigate to is a dead promise, which is why the cells-map detail and the postcard-invite allowance are listed as the two tiers' actual landing surfaces. The privacy mirror is home-gated, so the coordinate-leak promise is invisible to T1 saved-place accounts, exactly the cohort the pilot recruits. pantopus://homes/:id/privacy is not among the eight /homes children Android's DeepLinkRouter enumerates, so a future privacy push falls through to the dashboard. And the web CTA "Claim this address and be one of the first here" is hard-coded client-side, so flipping the server default to founding-closed fixes the label while the button keeps promising firstness.

Nothing here touches either Today screen: F9 is the only feature in this design that lands entirely outside the Today split, which is worth stating since every sibling feature has to declare it.

Effort: the doc's "two to three days total" holds only for the copy items. Three entries carry real design work — the curator chip across three card variants plus decode safety, the cells-map locked state, and the web rewards card — at roughly a platform-day each. That belongs in the build-order section, not hidden inside the estimate.

a22d2c741efcd00d7.lens: Data visualization and information design — what should be a mark instead of a string, what encoding makes two addresses comparable without judging a home, and how provenance (OFFICIAL vs UNVERIFIED) is encoded consistently across calendar, push, widget and share card.
a22d2c741efcd00d7.verdict: The screen set is a sound information architecture that treats every payload as prose. Four datasets in this repo already have real structure and every one of them ships as a string: a 14-day dated sequence (composeForHome), a 0–500 scalar with six canonical named bands (PlaceAirQualityData.index), a 12-month own-vs-peer money series with k-anon household counts (homeBillComparisonService — rendered as sentences on Android only, nothing on web/iOS), and a 5-slot/21-day founding window (cellFoundingWindow, collapsed to a boolean before it reaches any UI). The blocker is F8's compare token: it declares `g:{flood:"A",wildfire:"C",air:"B",radon:"D"}` while the actual fields are four incommensurable labels — `flood.risk_level`, `wildfire.hazard_label`, `air_quality.category_label`, `Zone N` (og/place/route.tsx:61-66, and note the helper there is named `grade` but returns a label). Letters manufacture a shared ordinal scale that does not exist, carry no legend, and convert "what's on record about an address" into a report card on a home — which is the exact thing the pilot's honesty bar scores at zero. Fix the encoding and most of the compare-layout problem dissolves: two readings on one instrument, not two scorecards. Second systemic problem: UNVERIFIED is expressed four different ways (a row-level string suffix, a parenthetical in push copy, a "·unconfirmed" glyph in the widget, and nothing at all on the compare card or OG image, whose token has no confidence field). That belongs in the mark — filled/hollow — not in repeated prose. Net screens: +1 (a year-at-a-glance timeline, +1; a large widget size, +1; one merged provenance sheet replacing three separate implementations, −1).

findings.problem: The compare token invents letter grades (A/C/B/D) for four layers whose real values are incommensurable labels from four different authorities: flood.risk_level (FEMA zone), wildfire.hazard_label (USFS class 1-5), air_quality.category_label (EPA AQI band), and 'Zone N' (EPA radon zone 1-3). A letter implies one scale, one direction and one legend, and there are none. It also reframes a public record as a score on someone's house — the precise reading the honesty bar counts at zero. A radar/spider is worse for the same reason plus one more: it normalizes four unlike axes onto one radius and encodes area, so a bigger blob reads as a worse home.
findings.recommendation: Drop letters entirely; no radar. Use four small-multiple SCALE STRIPS — one per layer, each drawn on its own source's named bands, stacked as four rows. Encoding: a horizontal track segmented into that authority's bands (flood: minimal / 100-yr / coastal; wildfire: USFS 1-5; air: EPA's 6; radon: zones 3-2-1), a marker positioned in the band, the band's plain-language name printed beside it, and the authority as the row caption ('FEMA flood zone', 'USFS wildfire hazard, quarter-mile', 'AirNow, today', 'County radon zone (EPA)'). The track never spans layers, so nothing sums or averages into a verdict. Fallback when a layer has no data: the track renders greyed with no marker and the words 'Not on record' — never a missing row, or the two compare columns silently differ in length. Add `conf` to the compare token and render an unverified reading as a hollow marker; if the token cannot carry confidence, drop unverified layers from the card rather than shipping them as confident.

findings.problem: The reveal is specified as two literal side-by-side cards. At 375px that is eight chips plus eight source captions, and the preview step is a fixed max-w-[540px] single column today. Two facing cards also make the comparison implicitly evaluative — two scorecards invite a winner — which is the neighbor-judgment failure mode.
findings.recommendation: One shared-scale comparison table: four rows, one per layer, each row a SINGLE track carrying BOTH marks — sender as a filled dot, 'You' as a ringed dot — with the layer name above and the two plain-language band values left and right beneath. This is the mark that makes the comparison read as two readings on one instrument rather than two verdicts, and it works identically at 375px and 1200px, which also solves the OG card. Order rows by distance between the two marks, descending, so the one real difference is row 1 — never a fixed order and never 'worse first'. Design the state the doc omits and that will be the most common outcome: both marks land in the same band, which should render as a merged mark and the words 'Both minimal' rather than two dots a pixel apart. Recipient geocode failure keeps the sender's marks on every track (the doc's own 'self-contained token' promise) instead of CouldNotPlace resetting the funnel. Reserve true two-column cards for >=768px only as a presentation of the same rows.

findings.problem: The address calendar is the product's signature dataset — a dated 14-day sequence with kind, confidence, source and lead_days per item — and every surface renders it as a vertical list of text rows. A list cannot answer the one question a two-week window exists to answer ('is anything happening this week, and when'), and it gives the empty state nothing to show but a sentence, so 'nothing on the calendar' is visually indistinguishable from a section that failed.
findings.recommendation: Keep the list for detail, but put a 14-DAY STRIP above it: 14 equal cells, today leftmost, weekday initial under each, a dot per event inside the day cell, colored by kind (pickup / civic / money / yours), max three dots then '+N'. Weekend cells tinted so the pickup cadence is legible as a rhythm rather than as a date. Marks: filled dot = official, hollow dot = unverified, dot with a tick = user-entered (see the provenance finding). This gives F4's 'tonight' row a spatial anchor (cell 2 emphasized, not an alert banner), gives F6's statewide election deadline a way to sit in the strip visually marked as not-this-address (a bar spanning the cell's full height rather than a dot), and gives the empty state 14 drawn-but-empty cells, which reads as 'checked, nothing found' instead of 'broken'. Fallback: section unavailable renders no strip at all, not an empty one.
