findings.problem: F5 captures dates that are annual by nature (lease_end, lease_notice, insurance_renewal, warranty_end, hoa_dues, tax_appeal) plus F6's election_deadline and F12's seeded county appeal windows, while composeForHome expands only 14 days. The proposed Your-dates card correctly fixes the 'my date vanished' bug, but a text list answers 'what did I enter', not 'when is my year busy' — which is the entire annual-return promise in the loop (step 6). There is no surface anywhere on which a user's own dates, their city's pickup cadence, their county's appeal window and their state's registration deadline appear as one thing.
findings.recommendation: Add one screen, 'The year at this address': a 12-month horizontal timeline, months as columns, with one LANE per source — You / Your city / Your county / Your state — and a marker per rule placed at its date. Today is a vertical rule; the 14-day window is a shaded band at the left so the card and this screen visibly show the same data at two zooms. Lane order puts 'You' on top so the user's own facts read as the foreground and seeded rows as context. Markers carry the provenance encoding (filled/hollow/tick) and tap into the merged provenance sheet. This is also the honest destination for the keeper's growth count and the natural home for a reminder lead indicator (a short leader line from the marker back to the reminder date). Fallback: fewer than two dated rules and the screen is not offered at all — the card suffices, and an almost-empty year reads as failure.

findings.problem: AQI is the one genuinely canonical scale in the entire product — PlaceAirQualityData.index is 0-500 with six universally recognized named bands — and it renders as a text chip, only when is_noteworthy is true (hub/today/page.tsx:242-246). So a healthy day and a failed fetch look the same (nothing), 'AQI 42 — Good' carries no sense of where 42 sits or how far 101 is, and F4's alert push lands on a screen that cannot show the crossing that caused it.
findings.recommendation: A six-band scale bar with a marker at the index: the EPA band colors (the one palette users already know from every other air app), the band name printed, dominant_pollutant as the caption, health_message below. Render it always, not only when noteworthy — the bar is what makes 'Good' informative. For the alert landing, mark the 101 threshold on the same bar so the push's cause is visible in one glance. Fallback: no reading renders the bar greyed with 'No reading for this address right now' — visibly distinct from a Good reading, which the current suppressed chip cannot be. On the medium widget this compresses to a ~100pt micro-bar with a marker, which says more than the string 'AQI 42 Good' in the same width.

findings.problem: Three equal text lines is the wrong information design for the smallest surface in the product, and it gives the user no reason to choose medium over small beyond 'more text'. The content is right; the encoding is not. Nothing in the proposal earns a size.
findings.recommendation: Make each size earn its area with a different form, not more strings. SMALL: one fact only — the nearest dated thing — with a kind glyph, the date word computed at render from the ISO date, and the provenance mark; no place label if it does not fit, no second line. MEDIUM: the medium earns the 14-day strip — 14 dot cells is roughly 120pt at 6pt cells and reads at a glance — as line 2, with pickup as the promoted line 1 and AQI as a micro band-bar with a marker instead of 'AQI 42 Good'. That division is honest and legible: small = one fact, medium = one fact plus the shape of the next two weeks. LARGE (missing, see missingScreens): the 12-month year strip plus today's three lines — the only place the annual-return promise is visible without opening the app. Staleness fallback: grey the marks but keep the strip geometry, so 'nothing due' (drawn cells, no dots) and 'stale' (dots, greyed) are different pictures; no snapshot at all shows the placeholder with no strip.

findings.problem: UNVERIFIED is encoded four incompatible ways for the same fact: a per-row string suffix ('· unconfirmed, please double-check', AddressCalendarCard.tsx:87), a parenthetical inside push copy, a '·unconfirmed' glyph in the widget, and nothing at all on the compare card or OG image — whose token schema has no confidence field, so a seeded unverified radon zone would unfurl in a chat thread as a confident grade. The prose approach fails on its own terms: it does not survive push truncation (the doc flags this itself), it cannot fit the OG card or a widget line, and repeated five times down a list it becomes boilerplate nobody reads — precisely where F4's honesty counter is scored.
findings.recommendation: Encode provenance in the MARK, once, everywhere: FILLED = official/confirmed, HOLLOW (outlined) = on record but unconfirmed, FILLED WITH A TICK = you entered it. Apply identically to the 14-day strip dot, the calendar row's icon tile, the year timeline marker, the AQI and scale-strip markers, the widget line glyph, and the compare track dot. Words then appear once per surface as a single legend line ('Hollow = on record, not yet confirmed'), not once per row. Keep exactly one prose exception: the push, where a mark cannot travel — and there the caveat belongs in the title suffix, not the body tail, so truncation cannot eat it. Data consequence to ship with it: add a confidence field to the compare token, or exclude unverified layers from the card. Accessibility: hollow/filled must be paired with a shape difference or a label, never color alone.

findings.problem: Two different quantities are about to wear the same meter. DensityCard already uses a 4-dot qualitative BUCKET_DOTS scale for 'verified homes nearby' — correctly k-anonymous, deliberately never a number. F8 then wants an exact '{slots_open} Founding Neighbor slots still open, closes {date}' from cellFoundingWindow (5 slots, 21-day window). If the founding line reuses dots, users will read the density dots as slots and vice versa; if it stays plain text, the one scarce, dated, countable thing in the product has no form at all.
findings.recommendation: Two visibly different meters. Density stays four qualitative dots with no count. Founding becomes a 5-SEGMENT SLOT METER (filled = taken, hollow = open, always exactly five segments so the denominator is visible) plus a thin window bar showing days remaining out of FOUNDING_WINDOW_DAYS=21. Hard fallback rule that F9 depends on: when the founding lookup fails or the window is closed, render NO METER — an empty 5-segment meter reads as 'five open', which is the exact false promise the fails-open fix exists to kill. Zero slots open shows no meter and no line, not a '0 of 5'.

findings.problem: A real 12-month own-vs-peer time series already exists — homeBillComparisonService returns own_months/amounts plus peer avg_amounts per bill_type with a household_count and an insufficientData flag — and it is rendered as sentences on Android only ('Neighborhood average: $84' per month, HomeIntelligenceComponents.kt:962-972) and as nothing at all on web and iOS. F10 stakes the monthly-return step of the loop on bills and never mentions this data.
findings.recommendation: Per bill_type: a 12-month column chart of your amount with the peer average as a single horizontal REFERENCE LINE — not a second series of paired bars. Paired bars invite a household-versus-household reading; a baseline reads as 'here is the going rate', which is what the k-anon peer average actually is. Current month highlighted; y-axis starting at zero since these are amounts; caption carries the k ('average of 14 homes nearby'). Fallback when insufficientData is true: draw the bars, omit the line entirely, caption 'Not enough homes nearby to compare yet' — the line's absence is the honest signal, and it must never degrade to a zero baseline. A snapped bill from F10 marks its column so the provenance block and the trend agree.

findings.problem: 'Ollie knows 6 things about this place' is a bare integer, and the proposed ledger renders it as a list of known/missing rows. Both undersell growth and, worse, a list of missing rows with CTAs is one visual step from the progress bar and completion percentage the design explicitly forbids.
findings.recommendation: Give the count a shape that has no completion semantics: a segmented RING of fact CATEGORIES — place, dates, money, people, proof — filled where anything is known in that category, hollow where nothing is, with the integer printed inside. Five segments, not ten rows, so nothing reads as 90% done; a category with one fact and a category with four look the same, which is the honest claim (the app knows about your money, not 'you are 60% complete'). T1 saved-place scope greys the categories that cannot exist there rather than showing them as missing, so a saved place reads as a smaller instrument, not a failing one. Fallback at zero: all segments hollow, 'Nothing on file yet', no illustration. The ledger rows stay underneath as the editing surface.

findings.problem: Three separate implementations of one idea are proposed: per-chip 'how we know' captions on the compare view, a calendar event detail sheet that explains source and confidence and lets the user dispute a date, and a bill provenance block explaining that a model read a photograph. They will diverge, and each one drawn separately is why provenance ends up as prose in some places and a glyph in others.
findings.recommendation: Merge into ONE provenance sheet, 'Where this comes from', parameterized by a common payload {value, scale_or_bands, authority, as_of, confidence, source_url, report_action}. Every mark in the system taps into it — a strip dot, a scale-strip marker, an AQI marker, a year-timeline marker, a bill's photo block. It is also the only place the honesty counter's 'not my schedule' report has a home, and building it once means the report affordance exists on every fact rather than only on calendar rows. This removes a screen from the inventory rather than adding one.

findings.problem: The design system ships a Sparkline primitive whose data is a hard-coded rising polyline (frontend/apps/web/src/components/archetypes/place/primitives.tsx:91-113: a literal points string, aria-hidden, no data prop). It is a decorative flourish with the name and shape of a chart. The moment anyone implements bill trends or the keeper's growth they will import it and ship an invented, always-rising trend line — a literal breach of the honesty rule with no test that would catch it, since nothing about it fails.
findings.recommendation: Before any of this visualization work lands: either give Sparkline a required `points: number[]` prop so it cannot render without data, or rename it DecorativeSparkline and add a lint rule or grep test forbidding it in any place/, home/ or hub/ data surface. One-line fix, and it is the cheapest honesty guarantee in the whole pack.

findings.problem: The four compare chips have no in-app twin: a recipient who signs up and wants to see 'my four layers properly' has nowhere to land, because /app/place/risk renders each layer as an independent inline chip row (presentation.tsx flood/wildfire/seismic/lead_radon entries) with no shared scale treatment.
findings.recommendation: Do NOT add a risk-profile screen. Make the existing risk section detail the in-app home of the same four scale strips used on the compare card, so the share artifact and the product are visibly the same instrument and the compare chips have a tap destination. Same component, three sizes: OG card, compare row, risk detail. This is the cheapest way to make the funnel's most-seen artifact feel like a preview of the app rather than a separate marketing object.

missingScreens.name: The year at this address (12-month dated timeline)
missingScreens.why: F5, F6 and F12 all create annual dates — lease end, notice deadline, insurance renewal, HOA dues, county appeal window, state registration deadline — while composeForHome expands 14 days, so the loop's annual-return step has no surface at all. A 12-month timeline with one lane per source (You / city / county / state), today as a vertical rule and the 14-day window shaded, is the only place a user can see that their year is busy in March, and the only place seeded county and state rows read as context rather than as unexplained rows in a card titled 'at this address'. It is also the honest destination for the keeper's fact count and for the reminder lead indicator.

missingScreens.name: Today widget — large size (iOS systemLarge / Android 4x4)
missingScreens.why: The proposal specifies only small and medium, both of which are text stacks; nothing earns a larger cell. Large is where the year strip plus today's three lines fit together, making the annual promise visible with no notification and no app open — which is exactly the return trigger F7 exists to provide for users who declined push. It also gives the widget gallery a reason to sell more than one size, and it needs its own drawing: a 12-month strip and a 14-day strip in one frame is a layout decision, not a scale-up of the medium.

aa3e46c7960859c43.lens: Information architecture: four-tab fit, merge pressure, and the T1/T3 fork
aa3e46c7960859c43.verdict: The proposed set is roughly 70 surfaces for a four-tab IA in which only two tabs (Place, Today) do any real work, and it is between 20 and 25 surfaces larger than the product needs. Three structural problems generate most of the excess. (1) "Today" names two different screens with two different payloads on every platform, so almost every feature is specified twice — F4, F5, F7 and F11 each carry a duplicate entry whose only reason to exist is the payload split. (2) There is no coherent "my place's facts" hub, so the same list of user-entered facts is drawn four times — as f2-first-week-checklist, f6-just-moved-card-synced, f5-your-dates-card and f11-keeper-knows-sheet — each with its own storage, its own dismissal and its own drift path. (3) "Tell the app a date" is specified as seven separate sheets (f5-add-date-sheet, f2-pickup-day-quick-set, f4-6-pickup-editor-entry, f6-voter-step-sheet, f12-calendar-event-detail-sheet, f5-remove-date-confirm, f10-3-extraction-confirm-sheet) when it is one sheet with modes. The T1/T3 split is worse than two parallel UIs: it is nine forks, three of them at the storage layer, and the doc has no migration that carries a user's dates, pickup rule, checklist ticks or keeper from SavedPlace.id to Home.id when they claim — so the highest-investment user loses everything they typed at the exact moment they invest most. That is a blocker, not a polish item. Net of my recommendations the set shrinks by about 23 surfaces while gaining one genuinely missing route (the place file) and one genuinely missing web route (bill detail, needed for push landings).

findings.problem: Two screens are named "Today" and they are different products. The Today tab renders GET /api/hub/today (weather, air, alerts, ranked signals, no home required); Place > Today renders GET /api/homes/:id/intelligence (address calendar, good-day tiles, sun, requires a claimed primary home). Every feature in this design has to declare which one it lands on, and four of them land on both, which is why the proposal contains duplicate entries: f5-t1-calendar-host exists only because the calendar card cannot reach the tab; f11-keeper-briefing-kicker exists only because the briefing is a third Today reachable only from a push; f4-7-tonight-row-address-calendar is f4-2-pickup-lead-card drawn again on the other payload. A user who claims their address watches the Today tab change layout wholesale and lose the calendar card, which reads as a regression.
findings.recommendation: One Today composition per platform. Move the address_calendar section into the hub payload (the backend already emits pickup there as a signal of kind 'address_calendar' at usefulnessEngine.js:310; the web type union HubTodaySignal.kind is simply missing the member) and drive section availability from data, not from which screen got mounted. Then stop calling /app/place/today and native Screen 2 "Today" — its unique content folds into the tab and the PlaceNavRail entry is deleted, or it is renamed "At this address" as a Place section. Land the briefing push on the Today tab with the delivered briefing pinned as the top card, which deletes the briefing detail screen as a separate destination and with it f11-keeper-briefing-kicker.

findings.problem: Nothing carries a user's investment across the T1→T3 boundary, and no surface admits it. F5 writes rules keyed scope_key = SavedPlace.id; claiming creates a Home with a new id. F11 stores the keeper in UserNotificationPreferences.settings at T1 and HomePreference.settings at T3 — two storage locations for one object. F2's checklist ticks and F6's just_moved_done live on HomeOccupancy, which does not exist at T1. §6 lists five migrations and none of them is a promotion or copy step. The result: the user sets a pickup day, a lease end and names their keeper as a saved-place user, claims the address, and everything they typed disappears — silently, at the moment of highest intent, with no screen that even acknowledges the transition.
findings.recommendation: Add a place-promotion step to the claim flow: copy AddressCalendarRule rows, the keeper object and the checklist ticks from scope ('saved_place', SavedPlace.id) to ('home', Home.id) inside the same transaction that creates the home, and surface the result on the existing VerifiedSuccess / post-claim screen as "Your pickup day, 2 dates and Ollie came with you." Store all place-scoped preferences in one slot keyed by (scope_type, scope_key) rather than splitting across HomePreference and UserNotificationPreferences. Until this exists, F5 and F11 should not ship to T1 at all.

findings.problem: "Tell the app a date" is designed as seven sheets. f5-add-date-sheet (kind + date + lead), f2-pickup-day-quick-set (weekday + frequency + next date, T1 only), f4-6-pickup-editor-entry (the same pickup control as a deep-link target, T3 only), f6-voter-step-sheet (a deadline + self-report), f12-calendar-event-detail-sheet (view/remind/dispute/edit one date), f5-remove-date-confirm, and f10-3-extraction-confirm-sheet (a date + amount + payee, whose lead picker the proposal says is "reused verbatim from F5"). The proposal half-notices this three times — "pickup could fold in as a seventh kind", "this sheet should be the SAME component F5 needs" — and then builds them separately anyway. Seven sheets means seven sets of loading/error/offline/permission states, seven tier-copy forks, and guaranteed divergence between the T1 pickup sheet and the T3 pickup editor.
findings.recommendation: One Date sheet, three modes and one kind list. Modes: create, view-mine (edit + remind + delete), view-seeded (read-only + source + remind + "this isn't right"). Kinds: the six F5 kinds, plus pickup day as a kind with a recurrence branch (weekday + frequency + explicit next date), plus bill as a kind pre-filled from OCR, plus election_deadline and tax_appeal as seeded read-only kinds. Scope ('home' | 'saved_place') is a prop, not a second component. f10-3 stays separate only because it is a per-piece capture step with a pinned photo — and it should then be a full screen in a capture→confirm→next loop, not a sheet over the triage list. Delete f5-remove-date-confirm in favour of delete + Undo (the pattern already ships at Android SavedPlacesScreen.kt:85-90).

findings.problem: There is no "my place's facts" hub, and as a result the same list is drawn four times with four different storage models and four different dismissals. f2-first-week-checklist asks for pickup day, a date and the household. f6-just-moved-card-synced lists pickup, mail, money, civic, block, register. f11-keeper-knows-sheet enumerates pickup day, lease end, notice deadline, insurance, warranty, HOA, bills, documents, co-residents and verification — which is the union of the other two plus F5's dates. f5-your-dates-card holds the subset the user typed. The proposal itself calls the keeper ledger "the durable form of the F2 checklist" and then keeps both. These will drift within one release: the checklist is keyed server-side in hub.js, Just Moved ticks live on HomeOccupancy, the keeper count is computed in GET /api/hub, and Your dates reads the calendar API.
findings.recommendation: Build one route — "Your place file" — in the Place tab, listing every fact the product can hold about this address: each row is either known (with its value and an edit affordance) or missing (with a CTA into the one Date sheet, the invite flow, docs or the verify sheet). Then: the first-week checklist becomes that route filtered to undone rows, surfaced on Today as a single progress row for 14 days, not a five-row card above the weather. Just Moved becomes the same route with the mover-only rows (mail forwarding, utilities, voter registration) enabled while move_in_date is recent — same ticks, same dismissal, one storage. "Ollie knows 6 things about this place" becomes the count of known rows and taps into the same route. f7-add-widget-nudge becomes a row in it rather than a promo on Today.

findings.problem: f1-location-source-sheet and f1-saved-places-list are the same screen specified twice. Both list the user's saved places, both mark which one Today is using, both offer use-for-Today / claim / remove, both carry an "Only you" line. The only difference is where they open from. Worse, neither has a nav entry: SavedPlaceContext renders bare in a 760px div from the ?savedPlace query branch with no PlaceShell and no rail, and no link anywhere in the web app points at it — so the surface the whole F1 bridge hangs on is unreachable, which makes F1's own acceptance criterion ("removing the last saved place returns Today to the starts-with-a-place state") untestable by a real person.
findings.recommendation: One Saved places surface. It is the Place tab's index for a user with no claimed home — which is the honest answer to "what is in the Place tab before you claim an address" — and it opens from the Today header chip as well. One row template with one "Used for Today" badge and one overflow. Kill the bare query-param frame; render it inside PlaceShell like every other Place surface so the badge is designed once, not twice.

findings.problem: Web carries four pairs of duplicated household surfaces with no cross-links, and the proposal extends one half of each pair. /app/homes/[id]/members and the 537-line dashboard Members & Security tab; /app/homes/[id]/settings and the 636-line HomeSettingsTab; the HomeAgenda calendar route (fully built, gated, read-only mode included, zero links anywhere in the app) and the dashboard CalendarCard's separate HouseholdCalendar 7-day aggregate; and /app/homes/[id]/members/add-guest, whose handleSubmit makes no network call and toasts success unconditionally. f3-members-roster proposes fixing the Invite button in one of the two members surfaces, which guarantees the pair diverges on the day it ships.
findings.recommendation: Collapse each pair before adding anything to it: /members becomes a thin wrapper over the dashboard tab (or the tab is deleted in favour of the route); same for settings; delete the dashboard's HouseholdCalendar aggregate and link the HomeAgenda route from the Home header tabs and the dashboard Calendar card — that is the cheapest win in F3 and it is what makes F3's calendar acceptance criterion pass on web at all. Delete /members/add-guest outright and point "Add guest" at the working Share Center; a form that fabricates success sits one tap from the flow F3 is trying to fix.

findings.problem: Household surfaces have no home in the four-tab IA. There is no Home tab; everything under /app/homes/[id]/* sits three taps deep under Place, and both natives auto-land on the Place dashboard. f3-who-lives-here-card is specified on the Home dashboard, which the proposal itself says "is not where anyone lands". f3-received-invitations is on My Homes, which a brand-new invitee with no home has no reason to open. The deep-link landings compound it: web has no bill detail route at all (the bills directory is one page.tsx), and Android's DeepLinkRouter.kt:551-570 enumerates eight /homes/:id children and sends everything else to the dashboard — so bill_paid, home_event_created, the F5 date reminder and the F10 bill reminder all mis-land on day one.
findings.recommendation: Make the Place tab's landing the place file (see the hub finding) with a "Household" block that carries the who-lives-here prompt, the member count and the pending-invite row — so the household's entry point is on the surface people actually land on, and the home dashboard becomes a detail view rather than a parallel home screen competing with Place. Add /app/homes/[id]/bills/[billId] on web (a few hours) so f3-bills-member-and-paid-landing, f10-5-bill-source-block and f10-7-bill-reminder-landing have an addressable target, and add the missing Android router branches for /bills, /calendar and /place/today?event= in the same PR as the notifications, not after.

findings.problem: Received invitations are designed twice (f3-received-invitations as a My Homes section, f3-invite-waiting-landing-entry as a banner on the landing surface) for the same job, and the proposal correctly says the first one's audience will never see it. Separately, the banner slot it targets is already contested by the verify banner and the setup banner with no precedence rule, and f2-first-week-checklist wants the same region.
findings.recommendation: One surface: the landing banner, with a stated precedence (invite > setup > verify) and a cap of one banner. When there are two or more invites it reads "You have 2 invitations" and opens a list — but that list is the existing /invite decision flow's index, not a designed My Homes section. Drop the My Homes section entirely; an invitation is an inbox item, and the person who has one usually has no home for My Homes to be about.

findings.problem: Two briefing opt-in cards are specified for the same screen — f1-briefing-optin-card (morning) and f4-4-evening-optin-card (night-before) — and the proposal then writes a uxRisk on each saying to show only one at a time. Their durable controls are also split across two entries (f1-briefing-settings, f4-5-notification-settings-evening-row) that edit adjacent rows of the same settings group. Meanwhile §5 counts evening_briefing_enabled toward activation and F4's whole feature rides it, so a morning-only card would make the activation bar unreachable for a navigation reason.
findings.recommendation: One briefing card with two switches — "A morning heads-up?" and "The night before pickup?" — expanding into one time-chip row each, reading OS notification authorization before it claims anything. One settings group holds both rows plus the pickup-status row. This also removes the ranking problem: for a user who declined push, the widget nudge (folded into the place file) is the better offer and can sit where the second card would have been.

findings.problem: The T1/T3 split produces nine forks, three of them at the storage layer, and they are the kind that drift invisibly: tier-dependent copy in f5-add-date-sheet; a whole second mount of the calendar in f5-t1-calendar-host; the same pickup control as a T1 sheet (f2-pickup-day-quick-set) and a T3 in-card editor (f4-6-pickup-editor-entry); a tier-gated household row in f2-first-week-checklist; two storage slots for the keeper in f11-keeper-naming-sheet; and three surfaces (f6-just-moved-card-synced, f9-privacy-mirror-post-location, the whole F10 set) that are home-gated by construction so the T1 user — the exact person F1 creates — never sees them.
findings.recommendation: There is a single-UI answer and it is a client-side one: resolve one `place` object at the top of the Place and Today trees — { scope: 'saved_place' | 'home', id, tier, capabilities: { can_edit_dates, shares_with_household, has_bills, can_verify } } — and pass it to every card. Tier changes copy and enables capabilities; it never changes which component is mounted, which screen the user is on, or where data is stored. Concretely that kills f5-t1-calendar-host and f2-pickup-day-quick-set as separate surfaces, and it makes the privacy mirror user-scoped rather than home-gated so the coordinate-leak promise is visible to the cohort the pilot actually recruits.

findings.problem: The design ships a nine-term vocabulary for one question — is this my house and can I prove it. Saved place, Home, claim, verify, address-verified, household-verified, legacy, Block Founder rank, Founding Neighbor tier, plus T1/T3/T4 in the copy. F3b adds two of these and F9 renames two more in the same release. f3-members-roster puts "Address-verified" / "Household member" chips on people's names in a roster of the people you live with, which reads as a social ranking of your housemates rather than as a capability note. No consumer arrives with any of these models.
findings.recommendation: Two user-facing states only: "Saved" and "Yours — verified". Never render the words tier, T1, household-verified or legacy. Replace the roster chip with a per-row capability note only where something is locked, and put the explanation on the action (f3b-attested-action-gating already proposes the right treatment: never hide, always explain, always offer the path) rather than on the person. Keep the F9 rank/tier rename but give them two visibly different chip shapes, or the rename changes nothing a reader perceives.

findings.problem: Notification preferences for this feature set are edited in four separate places, and two of them do not persist. f1-briefing-settings, f4-5-notification-settings-evening-row, f5-reminder-settings-copy and f3-household-notification-preferences all target rows of the same settings page; the per-home toggles at /app/homes/[id]/settings:157-167 are local useState with a "real impl would persist" comment; f10-8-mail-snap-privacy-card adds a fifth settings surface. Shipping three new notification types behind a control that pretends to save is worse than shipping no control.
findings.recommendation: One Notifications page, three groups: Briefings (morning, evening, times, pickup status), Household activity (bills paid, tasks completed, events added), Date and bill reminders (renamed from "Home Reminders", which misdescribes the toggle for a user with no home). Delete the fake per-home toggles rather than wiring them — decide now whether per-home granularity exists at all. Per-kind mute belongs on the date row itself ("Remind me: never"), not as new settings rows.

findings.problem: The keeper introduces two new mental models at once on the product's return surface: a creature whose mood is a summary of obligations, and a level/growth system ("knows 6 things about this place") with no streaks and no decay. The second is the useful half — it is the place file wearing a costume — and the first is decoration that, per the proposal's own reading of hub.js:221-260, will cheerfully render "relaxed" on the day a bill is overdue because the mail and bill counts swallow errors to zero.
findings.recommendation: Ship the place file first and let it stand alone. If the keeper ships after it, it is a name and a mood line on top of that file, not a second information architecture: drop the "knows N things" mechanic (the file already shows the facts) and make the mood nullable end to end with an explicit "Couldn't check what's due" state visually distinct from "relaxed". Keep f11-keeper-naming-sheet as an inline invitation on the strip that expands, never an auto-presented modal on the second open — that is the worst possible moment to ask someone who opened the app to learn whether recycling is tomorrow.

findings.problem: Three separate destructive confirmation dialogs are specified for single-row, reversible deletions: f1-remove-saved-place-confirm, f5-remove-date-confirm, plus keeper removal in the ledger overflow. The repo already has the better pattern shipped — optimistic delete with a 4-second Undo at Android SavedPlacesScreen.kt:85-90 — and the proposal argues for it in f5-remove-date-confirm's own uxRisk and then keeps the dialog anyway.
findings.recommendation: One destructive pattern: optimistic delete + Undo toast everywhere, with a one-line consequence prefix only in the two cases where something beyond the actor is affected — removing the saved place Today is running on, and removing a date other household members can see. No dialogs. Note the correctness dependency: the saved-place removal must invalidate queryKeys.hubToday, since both web Today mounts hold staleTime 120s and today the address keeps rendering for two minutes after removal — on a surface whose whole promise is "only you", that reads as a privacy failure.

findings.problem: Three proposed screens are too thin to deserve a route or a sheet. f9-earn-unavailable-landing is a route whose entire purpose is to say the feature is not here. f9-curator-explainer-sheet is four short lines plus a mute toggle. f1-post-save-arrival is a dedicated arrival screen whose content is a title swap, one sentence and three buttons.
findings.recommendation: Earn: redirect to the mailbox root with one neutral line, no route — and keep the wallet reachable for anyone with a balance rather than 404-ing a user out of their own money. Curator: make it "Why am I seeing this?" in the post overflow menu, expanding in place, with the mute writing to the feed preferences that already exist. Post-save: make it the success state of the save with the primary action going straight to Today; the one moment the user learns the bridge did anything does not need its own route.

findings.problem: Three proposed cards are secretly screens. f10-3-extraction-confirm-sheet is a pinned photo plus six editable fields of three different input types, per-field confidence, a lead picker, two commits and a duplicate warning — done N times per stack of mail, which is a screen on a phone, not a sheet. f8-2-compare-reveal is a two-column reveal with its own skeleton and its own error states that must not fall back to the hero (CouldNotPlace at StartFunnel.tsx:585-600 currently resets selected+submitted and would destroy the sender column) — that is a third state of the funnel state machine, not a card inside the preview step. f2-first-week-checklist is five rows, one of them two-line and tier-gated, sitting above the weather on the return surface for weeks.
findings.recommendation: Extraction confirm becomes a full-screen step in a capture → confirm → next loop. The compare reveal becomes an explicit third step of the StartFunnel state machine (hero | compare-reveal | preview) with its own two-column skeleton, and the recipient's geocode failure keeps the sender column rather than resetting. The checklist becomes one progress row on Today pointing at the place file. Reclassification, not addition — but each of these is currently budgeted as a card and will be built as one.

findings.problem: Nearby is the only tab the loop never touches — one card (f9-cells-map-detail-unlock) across roughly 70 surfaces — while block and founding content is split across two tabs: "Your block" and Block Founders live under Place (PlaceNavRail, f9-founding-name-block-detail), the cells map lives under Nearby, and f8-8-founding-same-block-line puts the founding window in the pre-auth wall. Either the fourth tab is dead weight during the pilot or it is the obvious home for this content.
findings.recommendation: Move all block and founding content to Nearby — cells map, Block Founders rank and roster, the postcard invite allowance (f9-postcard-invite-allowance), and the referral rewards card that currently has no home at all (f9-invite-rewards-card-web targets /app/profile, which is not one of the four tabs). Place > "Your block" becomes a pointer row. That gives the fourth tab a job and gives the two unlocked referral tiers real destinations, which the proposal correctly flags as dead promises today.

findings.problem: F10 puts one photographed bill in three lists with three different affordances — the Mail Day triage row, the bills list with f10-5-bill-source-block, and the mailbox drawer piece at f10-9-photographed-mail-piece — plus a fourth surface, f10-4-snap-photo-viewer, whose only job is to show and delete the image. The proposal defends the record/obligation split, which is sound, but four surfaces for one object is one too many.
findings.recommendation: Fold f10-4 into f10-9: the mail piece detail is the photo viewer — full-bleed image, who can see it, taken-on date, and the single destructive "Delete this photo" with its "the bill and its amount stay" confirm. The bill's provenance block links to the mail piece rather than opening a separate viewer. Two durable surfaces (the record in Mail, the obligation in Place > bills), cross-linked both ways, plus the transient triage row.

missingScreens.name: Your place file (Place tab route)
missingScreens.why: The single most important missing surface, and the answer to "is there a coherent my-place's-facts hub" — today there is not. Four proposed surfaces each show a slice of the same list (f2-first-week-checklist, f6-just-moved-card-synced, f5-your-dates-card, f11-keeper-knows-sheet) with four storage models and four dismissals. One route listing every fact the product can hold about this address — pickup day, the six date kinds, move-in date, bills, documents, co-residents, verification, widget placed — each row known-with-value or missing-with-CTA, is what the checklist, the mover's list, the keeper's count and the dates card all collapse into. It also gives the Place tab a reason to exist for a user with no claimed home.

missingScreens.name: Claimed — what came with you (promotion confirmation)
missingScreens.why: Nothing in the design acknowledges the T1→T3 transition on screen, and §6's five migrations contain no promotion step. Without a surface that says "your pickup day, 2 dates and Ollie came with you", the copy is either silently lossy or silently correct and untestable. Fold it into the existing post-verify VerifiedSuccess screen rather than building a route, but it must exist before F5 or F11 ship to saved-place users.

missingScreens.name: "This isn't right" dispute affordance and confirmation
missingScreens.why: §5's honesty counter is defined as "any user report tagged not my schedule", and f4-2-pickup-lead-card, f4-7-tonight-row-address-calendar and f12-calendar-event-detail-sheet each assume the report exists. There is no endpoint, no component and no confirmation anywhere in the product. One shared inline control plus a "Thanks — we'll check it" state, reusable by the pickup card, the seeded tax-appeal row and the election deadline. Small, but the pilot's single zero-target metric cannot be measured without it.

missingScreens.name: Web bill detail route (/app/homes/[id]/bills/[billId])
missingScreens.why: Web has no bill detail route at all — the bills directory contains only page.tsx. Four proposed surfaces need an addressable bill: f3-bills-member-and-paid-landing (the bill_paid deep link), f10-5-bill-source-block (provenance, photo entry, fix-what-we-read), f10-7-bill-reminder-landing, and the calendar row's tap target in f10-6-calendar-bill-items. Design rule 4 requires every push to deep-link to the exact surface; on web today it can only land on a list.

missingScreens.name: Privacy mirror for a saved place
missingScreens.why: f9-privacy-mirror-post-location is the only surface where the coordinate-leak fix becomes legible, and the mirror is home-gated on all three platforms — so the promise is invisible to exactly the T1 cohort F1 creates and the pilot recruits. Make the mirror user-scoped with a place selector rather than home-scoped, or the fix ships unfalsifiable from inside the product for the people most likely to be posting from a bookmarked address.

ae4a9f8ccb9240b56.lens: Adversarial end-to-end flow walk: every surface a real user lands on, including auth, OS permission, tier promotion, and failure paths
ae4a9f8ccb9240b56.verdict: Strong within features, blind between them. The set genuinely catches the big structural holes (F5's management list, F7's discovery surfaces, F3b's gating states, the two-Today split) and its per-entry state lists are better than the doc's. But it is organized feature-by-feature, so every remaining gap sits in a seam where one feature's output is another's input: account creation, OS permission grants, saved-place→home promotion, and correction durability. Walking the ten flows end to end, nine surfaces are missing and two of them break the pilot's headline metrics before any feature is at fault — the email-verification step silently destroys the saved place the whole bridge depends on (flow 1), and iOS burns its one-shot notification permission at app launch, before the user has a place or a reason (flow 2). Flow 10 (saved place then claim) has no surface anywhere in the set despite being the most likely path for a mover. Flow 6's "Preview an address" CTA has no destination at all on Android. The set is roughly 80% of the real screen count; the missing 20% is where users get stuck with no way forward.

findings.problem: Flow 1 has undesigned surfaces between account creation and Today, and one of them destroys the saved place. `app/(auth)/register/page.tsx:132` routes to `/verify-email-sent` after signup, but the previewed address is stashed in localStorage with a 24h TTL and an explicit same-device-only comment (`components/place/pendingPlace.ts`, PREFIX `pantopus:place-preview:`). A user who registers on a laptop and opens the verification email on their phone — or on mobile web where the mail app opens a different in-app browser — arrives with the draft gone, lands on /app/place with no preview and no saved place, and Today shows 'Today starts with a place'. The bridge silently fails for the single most common signup path, and f1-post-save-arrival is the only entry in the set covering this stretch.
findings.recommendation: Add two surfaces and one backend change. (a) The verification interstitial and the verification landing must carry the held address label (never coordinates) — 'We're holding 1402 NE 3rd Ave for you. Verify your email to save it.' (b) On arrival at /app/place?preview=<id> with an unreadable or expired draft, show a recovery state that keeps the promise — 'We couldn't find that preview on this device' with the address field inline and a one-tap re-save — instead of dropping to the generic empty Place. (c) The real fix: persist the pending place server-side against the unverified account at register time so verification on any device completes the bridge; the localStorage draft then becomes an optimization, not the load-bearing path.

findings.problem: The correction the whole of F4 depends on does not take at T1, and the set treats it as shipped. `SCOPE_RANK` in backend/services/addressCalendarService.js:25 is `{ home: 0, city: 1, county: 2, state: 3 }` — no `saved_place`. `applyPrecedence` (:74-83) skips any rule whose scope has no rank when computing the best rank, then filters with `SCOPE_RANK[r.scope_type] === bestRank.get(r.kind)`, so a saved_place pickup rule is dropped entirely whenever a city rule exists for that kind. Separately, `hasHouseholdPickup` (:112) matches only `scope_type === 'home'`, so a saved_place garbage rule never suppresses the guessed city week. Net: a T1 user taps 'That's my day', saves, and the card still shows the city's Thursday with '(unconfirmed, please double-check)' — their own day is invisible. Lease/insurance dates survive only because no city rule shares those kinds.
findings.recommendation: Extend SCOPE_RANK with `saved_place: 0` and widen the hasHouseholdPickup test to `scope_type === 'home' || scope_type === 'saved_place'` in the same migration as the scope CHECK — this is a backend line item F5 does not list. On the surface side, the confirmation must be visible and durable, not a toast: the calendar row flips from 'City schedule · unconfirmed' to 'You · Tuesday' and the caveat disappears. Add an explicit post-confirm state to f4-2, f4-7 and f5-calendar-card-dates, and add a test asserting the city rule is suppressed at saved_place scope before f2-pickup-day-quick-set ships.

findings.problem: iOS spends its one-shot notification permission at app launch, before any value is shown. `Pantopus/App/AppDelegate.swift:50-61` calls `requestNotificationPermission()` from `didFinishLaunchingWithOptions`, firing the system prompt on cold first launch — before the user has a place, before the aha, before any briefing is offered. Every push in the design (F4 pickup, F5 date reminders, F3 co-resident activity, F4 alerts) depends on a grant the app burns at the worst possible moment, and iOS never re-asks. The set treats this as a state ('OS notification permission denied') on f1-briefing-optin-card and f4-4, but a denied user has no path back inside the product and the activation metric counts briefing-on.
findings.recommendation: Add a pre-permission primer sheet on both natives, presented at the moment of the briefing opt-in (or the first pickup confirmation), not at launch — 'We'll tell you the night before pickup. Nothing else.' with Yes/Not now, and only then the OS prompt. Move the AppDelegate call behind it. Add a denied-recovery row to the briefing settings and to both opt-in cards: 'Notifications are off for Pantopus' + Open Settings, and rank f7-add-widget-nudge above the briefing opt-in for denied users, since the widget is the only return trigger that needs no permission.

findings.problem: 'Preview an address' has no destination for a signed-in user on Android, so flow 6 and the F1 empty state both dead-end. The Place launch funnel (PlaceLaunchScreen.kt) is the signed-out root; Android's only saved-place write path is HomeTabHostViewModel.save() reading a pending draft from the signup flow. A signed-in Android user with no place — exactly the person who adds the widget (flow 6), or who declines the claim at signup — can tap 'Preview an address' on f1-today-empty, or tap the widget's 'Save an address to see today here', and reach nothing. iOS is better off only because SavePlaceSheet.swift exists, but the set names no entry point to it either.
findings.recommendation: Add a signed-in add-a-place sheet on Android (address autocomplete + save, reusing SavedPlacesApi which already exists) and wire iOS's existing SavePlaceSheet to the same entry points. Both f1-today-empty-starts-with-a-place and f7-widget-tap-landing must route to it, not to the signed-out launch funnel or to 'Claim your address' — which is a different, heavier promise than the copy makes. Until it exists, the widget must not advertise 'Save an address to see today here' on Android.

findings.problem: Flow 4's upgrade path may terminate in a sheet whose every method fails. f3b-attested-action-gating promises 'never hide, always explain, always offer the path', and f3b-verify-address-sheet is that path — but neither entry establishes that a second resident of an ALREADY-CLAIMED home can complete any verification method. Postcard code goes to the address (a co-resident may not handle mail), document review wants a lease in their name (often only one signer), landlord confirmation needs the landlord. If none accepts a non-owner occupant on a home someone else has claimed, then every locked control an invited co-resident taps leads to a sheet that cannot be completed — a worse outcome than hiding the control, and the exact 'stuck with no way forward' case.
findings.recommendation: Before the F3b gate ships, confirm which verification methods accept a non-owner occupant on a claimed home. If any do, say so explicitly in the sheet's method rows with their requirements. If none do, the sheet needs a distinct state — 'This address is already verified by {owner}. Ask them to confirm you live here.' — plus an owner-side approval surface ('Confirm this person lives here') that writes verification_source='address'. Ship that surface with the migration, or hold f3b-attested-action-gating, because flipping isVerifiedResident to false without a completable path strands every invited co-resident.

findings.problem: Flow 10 has no surface anywhere in the set. When a saved-place user later claims the same address, five things change silently and simultaneously: resolveLocation flips to the home so Today's payload and the 'Saved place · Only you' chip change; the F5 dates written at scope_key=SavedPlace.id become invisible because Today #2 reads home scope; the keeper object lives on UserNotificationPreferences.settings keyed by the saved place and has no home twin, so the named creature resets; the widget's placeLabel changes under a snapshot nobody rewrote; and the SavedPlace row survives, so the saved-places list shows the same address twice. The set flags the data question in f5-t1-calendar-host's uxRisk and f11's rationale but proposes no screen, and this is the modal path for a mover who previews before they move.
findings.recommendation: Make the existing VerifiedSuccess screen (/app/place?verified=1, PlaceDashboard route branch) the host — it is the natural receipt moment and no entry in the set touches it. Add a 'what came with you' block: the dates that moved to household scope, the keeper's name kept, and one line that the private bookmark is now a home others in the household can see (a real privacy delta: T1 dates were 'Only you', T3 dates are household-visible — that change needs consent, not a silent migration). Server-side, copy saved_place rules to home scope on claim and retire the duplicate SavedPlace row, or the user loses the dates at the moment of maximum investment. Also add the 'claimed' row state to f1-saved-places-list.

findings.problem: Flow 2's notifications-off path has no destination on either native, and the set explicitly declined to add one ('Deliberately not invented: a briefings history/list screen'). TodayTabRoot mounts TodayDetailView only when a push supplied a deliveryId (RootTabView.swift:257-263); Android's Today tab renders the intelligence payload. f4-2-pickup-lead-card and f4-3-quiet-day-state both live on Today #1, so a native user who declined push, or who simply swiped the notification away before opening it, can never see the pickup card or the 'nothing needs you today' receipt. Design rule 4 ('every push has an in-app equivalent that works with notifications off') fails on two of three platforms, and f4-7 is the only fallback — a row inside a card on a home-gated screen.
findings.recommendation: Pick one and name it as a surface: either the native Today tab hosts Screen 1 content for all users (which F1 already forces for T1, so the second payload branch is being built anyway — extend it to home users rather than splitting the tab by tier), or add a notification-centre row for delivered briefings that reopens TodayDetailView by deliveryId. The first is cheaper and removes the two-Today split on natives rather than deepening it.

findings.problem: Flow 3's second-warranty case is data loss presented as a choice. f5-add-date-sheet's replace state ('You already set Lease ends for Mar 31, 2027. Replace it?') is the only answer to 'one row per kind', but at T3 the doc names a real alternative the sheet never offers (a second warranty goes into HomeCalendarEvent), and at T1 there is no alternative at all. Worse, with only a kind and an optional title, the warning cannot tell the user WHICH warranty they are about to overwrite unless it renders the stored title — so a user replaces 'Fridge warranty' believing they are adding 'Car warranty'.
findings.recommendation: Render the existing row's title and date in the replace warning, not just the kind. At T3 add a third action — 'Add as a separate calendar event' — routing to the household calendar create sheet, which f3-household-calendar-entry is already giving an entry point. At T1 state the limit honestly in the kind picker before the user types ('Warranty ends — one per place for now; already set for Fridge warranty, Nov 2') rather than after. Never let Replace be the only path forward on a destructive collision.

findings.problem: Flow 5's sender-side reissue row has no entry point, so the INVITE_POLICY_CHANGED loop stays open. f3-invite-policy-reissue designs both halves correctly, but nothing tells the sender it happened: the migration invalidates pending invites silently, and a sender has no reason to open Members > Pending. The recipient is told to 'ask {inviter} to send a new one' — to a person who sees nothing wrong on any screen they visit. f3-invite-waiting-landing-entry solves exactly this discovery problem for the recipient side and has no sender twin. Separately, a signed-out recipient who hits a policy-changed invite and then registers has no designed return to the invite.
findings.recommendation: Emit an in-app Notification to the sender on reissue-required ('2 invitations need to be sent again') and give it a row in the same single-slot landing banner precedence f3-invite-waiting-landing-entry defines (invite > reissue > setup > verify). For the signed-out case, preserve the invite token through the register redirect and land back on the decision screen, which is the same redirect-preservation the register page already does for /start previews.

findings.problem: Flow 9 cannot be completed: there is no preference anywhere for the alert pushes, and F4 widens exactly those to saved-place users. AQI ≥ 101 and NOAA alerts come from alert_checker.py, gated by no user-facing switch; f4-8-saved-place-alert-push acknowledges this is the first push a T1 user ever receives, about an address they merely bookmarked, and proposes no off switch. A user asking for 'fewer pushes, only the pickup one' can turn off morning briefing, keep evening, and kill all bill/task/date reminders via the single home_reminders toggle — and still receive unmutable air and weather alerts. Compounding it, the master gate for home pushes is MailPreferences.push_notifications, which lives in the Mail area, so the switch that silences household pushes is not on the notifications screen at all.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Air and weather alerts' row (with a severity threshold, not just on/off) to the notification settings group on all three platforms, and state in f4-8's landing copy which saved address triggered it. Surface the MailPreferences master on the notifications screen as the visible top-level gate rather than leaving it in Mail. Also split the single home_reminders toggle into bills/tasks vs dates, since F5 introduces a reminder class the user cannot mute without losing bill reminders.

findings.problem: Flow 4's first co-resident session is undesigned, and three surfaces will misfire on it. Accepting an invite writes HomeOccupancy, which resolveLocation reads — so that address instantly becomes their Today with no explanation. On the Place dashboard the T3 verify banner fires at someone who just 'verified' by invitation; JustMovedCard is gated on Home.move_in_date, which belongs to the owner, so a co-resident who moved in two years later may be shown a first-week checklist; and f2-first-week-checklist shows 'Verify you live here' to a household-verified member for whom that step means a second, different verification they may not be able to complete (see the blocker above). The set designs the accept moment (f3b-invitation-decision) and the dashboard (f3-member-home-dashboard) but not the session in between.
findings.recommendation: Define the household-verified variant of each: the F2 checklist drops or re-labels 'Verify you live here' for verification_source='household' (it is an upgrade, not a setup step, and belongs in f3b-verify-address-sheet's entry points); JustMovedCard keys on the viewer's own HomeOccupancy.start_at, not Home.move_in_date; and the Place dashboard's first load after accept says which address Today now uses and why, reusing f1-location-source-sheet rather than changing silently.

findings.problem: Flow 8 ends on a screen that does not exist, and 'mark paid' now has three write sites with different semantics. f10-7-bill-reminder-landing requires landing on the bill itself, but web has no bill detail route (the bills directory contains only page.tsx) — f10-5 notes this as a recommendation rather than a requirement. Meanwhile mark-paid will exist on the bills list, the dashboard bills card, and the new f10-6 calendar row, where the set proposes optimistic-paid-with-undo; three paths to one irreversible-feeling financial write, with the undo window present on only one of them, and F3's bill_paid notification firing from all three.
findings.recommendation: Add /app/homes/[id]/bills/[billId] as a thin web route — it is a few hours and it is the landing target for f10-7, the destination for F3's bill_paid notification, and the host for f10-5's provenance block and the f10-4 photo entry point. Then make undo semantics identical across all three write sites, or remove the write from the calendar row entirely and have it open the bill (the calendar is a glanceable surface; a mis-tap there should not mark a household bill paid and notify everyone).

findings.problem: Flow 1's first sixty seconds have a third Today branch nobody separates. A brand-new saved place is a cold geohash: the provider fan-out may return partial or empty on the first request. f1-today-empty-starts-with-a-place correctly splits source==='none' from display_mode==='hidden', but not from 'we have a location and nothing has resolved yet' — and f4-3-quiet-day-state's all-clear copy ('Nothing needs your attention today') would be a lie in that window, since its own receipt line claims the checks succeeded. The first Today a new user ever sees is the single highest-stakes render in the loop and it is the one most likely to be empty.
findings.recommendation: Add a warming state to f1-today-saved-place-mode: location resolved, sections pending — 'Setting up Today for {label}' with the sections that have arrived rendering as they land, and no all-clear claim until every check reports. Make f4-3's quiet-day receipt line the gate: if any check has not completed, the screen is warming, not quiet. Assert it in the web savedPlaceContext test with a stubbed partial payload.

findings.problem: Flow 7's reciprocal compare has no state, and the likeliest recipient is asked to sign in again. f8-3-compare-sheet is hosted 'under the AhaCard in PreviewBody' with no mention of the ?vs= reveal context, so a recipient who wants to send their own card back has no described affordance at the moment they want it. Separately, /start is the public funnel: a signed-in pilot user opening a friend's compare link gets PlaceHeader's 'Sign in' rightSlot (StartFunnel continueWithPreview('/login')) — the most likely recipient in a 30-mover pilot is told to sign in to an account they are already in.
findings.recommendation: Make f8-3 explicitly available in the reveal with reciprocal copy ('Send yours back'), and add a signed-in variant of the funnel header: swap 'Sign in' for 'Save this address' / 'Open Today' and skip the wall. Neither needs a new screen, but both are states the entries do not list, and the spread metric is measured on exactly this path.

findings.problem: Two different report affordances are proposed for the same act, with no endpoint and no confirmation surface behind either. f4-2 and f4-7 offer 'Not my schedule' (described as filing the report the §5 honesty counter reads); f12-calendar-event-detail-sheet offers 'This isn't right' and flags the missing backend. §5 counts 'any user report tagged not my schedule' as one of two honesty inputs, so the metric currently has two half-built front doors and no back end.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one report sheet taking (rule_id, reason) with a single confirmation ('Thanks — we'll check it'), reachable from the pickup card, the tonight row and the event detail sheet, and name the endpoint as a backend line item in F4 rather than F12 — the honesty counter is an F4 acceptance criterion.

findings.problem: Flow 8's 'find the photo again' works only while the user remembers roughly when they snapped it. f10-9 puts photographed pieces in the chronological mailbox drawers with a badge or filter; there is no search by payee or amount, and f10-5's provenance block is reachable only from the bill. A user looking for 'the photo of the water bill from July' walks a dated list.
findings.recommendation: Give the photographed-mail filter in f10-9 a payee/amount search, or make f10-8's storage card list snaps with their extracted payee and date — it already renders a count and a bulk delete, so listing what will be deleted is both the finder and the honest precondition for the destructive action.

findings.problem: Flow 10's variant — a user who saved one address and later claims a different one — switches Today silently. Because a home outranks a saved place in resolveLocation, the address on Today changes with no notice, and f1-location-source-sheet's chooser correctly disables the saved place as outranked but nothing announces the switch at the moment it happens.
findings.recommendation: One-time notice on the first Today after a claim: 'Today now uses {home label}. {saved label} is still saved.' tapping into f1-location-source-sheet. Reuse the same slot as the post-claim receipt from the flow-10 finding above so it is one surface, not two.

missingScreens.name: Email-verification handoff carrying the held address (verify-email-sent + verify-email landing)
missingScreens.why: Flow 1. register/page.tsx:132 routes to /verify-email-sent, and the previewed address lives in a device-local localStorage draft (pendingPlace.ts, 24h TTL). Verifying on a second device loses the place and the bridge never happens. The interstitial must name the held address and the landing must complete the save from the server-side draft.

missingScreens.name: Preview-lost recovery on the post-signup arrival
missingScreens.why: Flow 1. When readPendingPlace returns null (expired, cleared, different device, storage blocked), the arrival screen has nothing to save and the user drops into a generic empty Place with no explanation and no way back to the address they typed. Needs an inline re-entry, not an empty state.

missingScreens.name: Notification permission primer + denied recovery
missingScreens.why: Flow 2. AppDelegate.swift:50-61 fires the iOS system prompt at app launch, spending the one-shot grant before the user has a place or a reason. Every push in F4/F5/F3 depends on it and iOS never re-asks. The primer belongs at the briefing opt-in; the recovery row belongs in settings and on both opt-in cards.

missingScreens.name: Signed-in add-a-place sheet (address search + save)
missingScreens.why: Flows 1 and 6. The Place launch funnel is the signed-out root; Android's only save path reads a pending draft from signup. So f1-today-empty's 'Preview an address' and the widget's 'Save an address to see today here' both dead-end for a signed-in Android user with no place. iOS has SavePlaceSheet but no entry point from these surfaces.

missingScreens.name: Claim-success receipt: what moved with you
missingScreens.why: Flow 10. Claiming a previously saved address silently changes Today's payload and chip, orphans saved_place-scoped dates, resets the keeper, restates the widget label, and leaves a duplicate saved-place row. It also flips those dates from 'Only you' to household-visible, which is a privacy change that needs consent. The existing VerifiedSuccess screen (/app/place?verified=1) is the untouched natural host.

missingScreens.name: Native entry point to the briefing content (Today tab hosts Screen 1, or a delivered-briefings row)
missingScreens.why: Flow 2. TodayDetailView mounts only from a push deliveryId, so a native user with notifications off — or who swiped the push away — can never reach f4-2's pickup card or f4-3's quiet-day receipt. Design rule 4's in-app equivalent fails on iOS and Android.

missingScreens.name: Web bill detail route (/app/homes/[id]/bills/[billId])
missingScreens.why: Flow 8. f10-7's reminder landing, F3's bill_paid notification, f10-5's provenance block and the f10-4 photo entry point all need a bill-shaped destination; web has only a list page, so every one of them lands on a list instead of the bill.

missingScreens.name: Owner-side 'confirm this person lives here' approval
missingScreens.why: Flow 4. f3b's upgrade path assumes a co-resident can complete address verification on a home someone else already claimed. If postcard, document and landlord flows do not accept a non-owner occupant there, every locked control leads to an uncompletable sheet — an owner-attestation path is the only way out.

missingScreens.name: Single 'this isn't right' report sheet
missingScreens.why: Flows 2 and 3. Two affordances are proposed for the same act ('Not my schedule' on the pickup card, 'This isn't right' on the event sheet) with no endpoint and no confirmation behind either, yet §5's honesty counter reads exactly this report as one of its two inputs.

a4b60daa5017e7225.headline: 59 surfaces, but only 5 of them are genuinely new screens: the loop needs one place file, one Date sheet, one Today, one provenance mark — plus 10 sheets, 14 new cards, 2 widget sizes-in-one and 28 extensions of screens that already ship, which is 159 per-platform builds across web, iOS and Android.

inventory.name: Where this comes from (provenance + "this isn't right")
inventory.feature: Cross-cutting (F4, F5, F6, F8, F9, F10, F12)
inventory.hostSurface: Opened from any data mark in the product: a 14-day strip dot, a calendar row, an air-quality marker, a compare scale strip, a bill provenance block, a seeded civic/tax row.
inventory.purpose: One sheet that answers 'where did this fact come from, how sure are we, and how do I tell you it's wrong' — so provenance is a mark everywhere and prose in exactly one place.
inventory.contents: Takes a common payload {value, bands, authority, as_of, confidence, source_url, rule_id}. Renders: the value in plain language; the authority ('FEMA flood zone', 'AirNow, today', 'Clark County Assessor', 'You', 'We read this from your photo'); observed/updated time; the confidence line ('On record, not yet confirmed'); a source link that opens in a new tab / SFSafariViewController / Custom Tab; and the report control 'This isn't right' with a two-option reason picker (wrong date / not my schedule) and the confirmation 'Thanks — we'll check it.' Needs a backend report endpoint that does not exist today.
states: no source_url (label, no dead tap target)
entryPoints: Any hollow or filled mark on the Today 14-day strip
inventory.visualization: A half-sheet whose top is the mark itself, rendered large, in the same three shapes used everywhere else: FILLED = official/confirmed, HOLLOW = on record but unconfirmed, FILLED-WITH-TICK = you entered it. Under it, a one-line legend, the authority as a caption, and the source link as a row with an external-link glyph. The report control is a quiet text button, not a destructive red.
inventory.uxNote: This resolves the single worst inconsistency across the three critiques: UNVERIFIED is currently specified four ways (a row-suffix string, a push parenthetical, a widget glyph, and nothing at all on the share card). Words repeated per row become boilerplate exactly where the pilot's zero-target honesty metric is scored; a shape repeated per mark does not. Push copy is the only exception — a mark cannot travel in a notification tray, so the caveat rides the title, never the body tail where truncation eats it. Build this FIRST: every other entry renders its marks.

inventory.name: The Date sheet (one sheet, three modes, ten kinds)
inventory.hostSurface: Presented over the Today tab, over the place file, and from a reminder deep link. Web: SlidePanel pattern. iOS: .sheet. Android: ModalBottomSheet.
inventory.purpose: 'Tell the app a date' is one job. Today it is specified as seven separate sheets; this is the one component that creates, shows, edits, reminds about and deletes every dated fact at an address.
inventory.contents: Modes: CREATE, VIEW-MINE (edit / remind / delete), VIEW-SEEDED (read-only, source, remind, dispute). Kinds: pickup day (with the recurrence branch — weekday, frequency not_set/weekly/biweekly, explicit next recycling date, never inferred), lease ends, notice deadline, insurance renews, warranty ends, HOA dues, property-tax appeal, voter-registration deadline (seeded, state-scoped), and bill (phase 2, pre-filled from OCR). Fields: kind, date picker (must accept ~2 years out), optional title, 'Remind me' 60/30/7/1 days. Scope ('home' | 'saved_place') is a prop, not a second component: it changes the footer line — 'Only you will see this.' vs 'Everyone in this household will see this.' — and nothing else. Seeded mode adds plain-language explanation ('Your county lets you challenge the assessed value your tax is based on'), the per-method dates for voter registration, and 'I did this' as a labelled self-report.
states: already-set collision — shows the existing row's TITLE and date, not just the kind, with Replace / Add as a separate calendar event (T3) / Cancel
validation: past date; lead longer than the distance to the date
deleted with Undo toast (no confirm dialog)
entryPoints: Place file: any missing-fact row CTA
Place file: any known-fact row tap (edit)
Today pickup card 'Not my schedule' / 'Set your pickup day'
inventory.visualization: Kind picker as a two-column grid of glyph tiles (one tap, no wizard step) above a native date control; the 'Remind me' row is a four-segment control where the chosen lead renders as a small leader line back to the date, so the reminder is visibly earlier than the event rather than an abstract number. Seeded mode shows the hollow provenance mark beside the date and the authority as a caption. The collision warning renders the conflicting row inline, marked, so the user sees exactly which warranty they are about to overwrite.
inventory.uxNote: The critiques split on whether pickup day is its own control. It is not: making it a kind with a recurrence branch is what unblocks F2's checklist row at T1 (where no pickup control exists at all today) and gives F4's push caveat a one-tap destination. Two backend blockers must ship with this or the sheet silently lies: (1) SCOPE_RANK in addressCalendarService.js:25 has no 'saved_place', so a T1 user's confirmed pickup day is dropped whenever a city rule exists for that kind — their correction is invisible; (2) the lead_days CHECK is 0–30 and the only value anyone picks for a lease notice is 60. Delete-with-Undo replaces all three proposed destructive dialogs (the pattern already ships at Android SavedPlacesScreen.kt:85-90).

inventory.name: Your place file
inventory.hostSurface: The Place tab's index — what the Place tab shows for a user who has saved an address, and the 'facts' destination for a user who has claimed one. Web /app/place; iOS HubTabRoot place root; Android root/home.
inventory.purpose: The one hub for every fact the product can hold about this address — so the first-week checklist, the mover's checklist, the user's dates and the keeper's 'knows N things' are one list with one storage model instead of four that drift.
inventory.contents: A 12-month year band at the top; below it, fact rows grouped in five categories — Place (address, pickup day, move-in date), Dates (the six F5 kinds + seeded county/state rows), Money (bills, phase 2), People (co-residents, invites), Proof (address verification). Each row is either KNOWN (value + edit affordance) or MISSING (one-line ask + CTA into the Date sheet, the add-a-place sheet, the invite composer, docs or the verify sheet). Mover rows (mail forwarding, utilities, voter registration) appear only while move_in_date is within 60 days. A 'Put today on your home screen' row appears when no widget is placed. Ticks and dismissals persist server-side (HomeOccupancy at T3, user preferences keyed by saved place at T1).
states: T1 saved place (Money/People/Proof rows render as 'Not here — this is a saved place', never as failures)
all known ('Everything we can hold about this place is on file' — no confetti, no percentage)
dismissed mover rows with an undo and a restore row in home settings
sync merge from another device shown once as 'Synced 3 items from your other device'
permission-denied per row (household member without finance.view / members.manage sees the fact counted, CTA disabled with the reason)
entryPoints: Place tab (it is the tab's index)
Today: a single progress row during the first 14 days ('3 of 6 things on file →')
Reminder pushes with no specific rule
inventory.visualization: Top band: a 12-month horizontal timeline, months as columns, with one LANE per source — You / Your city / Your county / Your state — a marker per rule at its date, today as a vertical rule, and the next 14 days shaded so the band and the Today strip are visibly the same data at two zooms. Markers carry the filled/hollow/tick provenance encoding. Below: fact rows, known rows showing the value as the primary line; missing rows showing the ask, not a red X. The category count renders as a five-segment ring (segment filled if anything is known in that category) with the integer inside — deliberately NOT a progress bar or percentage, so nothing reads as 'you are 60% complete'.
inventory.uxNote: This is the single largest merge in the pack and the most important one for a first-time user: today the same list of facts is drawn as F2's checklist, F6's Just Moved card, F5's Your-dates card and F11's keeper ledger, with four storage models and four dismissals. One route also fixes two structural holes — the Place tab has no reason to exist for a user with no claimed home, and F5's own acceptance criterion is false today because composeForHome expands only 14 days, so a lease end eight months out is saved, toasted, and then invisible and undeletable until two weeks before it fires. The year band is what makes the loop's annual-return step visible at all.

inventory.name: Your places (and which one Today uses)
inventory.hostSurface: Web: SavedPlaceContext, re-hosted inside PlaceShell (kill the bare 760px query-param frame at app/(app)/app/place/page.tsx:43-44). iOS: Features/SavedPlaces. Android: ui/screens/saved_places/SavedPlacesScreen.kt.
inventory.purpose: See everything you saved, see which one Today is running on and why, switch it, claim it or remove it — in one surface instead of the two the doc specifies.
inventory.contents: Rows of label + city/state + saved date; a 'Used for Today' badge on the resolved place; the precedence explanation in one sentence ('Today uses the address you saved most recently' / 'A home you've claimed always wins'); row overflow (Open, Use for Today, Claim this address, Remove); a header line 'Only you can see these.'; and an empty state pointing at the add-a-place sheet. 'Use for Today' writes the existing UserNotificationPreferences custom pin, which already outranks everything in resolveLocation — no new column.
states: a home outranks the saved place (selection disabled, explained)
row already claimed (renders as a home, not a saved place)
entryPoints: Place tab when there is no claimed home
Today header chip ('Saved place · Only you' → opens here)
inventory.visualization: A list where exactly one row carries a filled 'Used for Today' badge and the rest carry nothing — one badge slot, one overflow, no chips competing. The precedence sentence sits directly under the badged row, not in a header, so the explanation is adjacent to the thing it explains. A claimed row renders with the home glyph and a greyed 'Today always uses your home' caption rather than a disabled-looking control.
inventory.uxNote: The doc specifies this twice (a saved-places list and a 'where Today gets this' sheet) for one job; merging them removes the worse failure, which is that the web saved-place surface has NO nav entry anywhere and renders frameless — so a web user who saves a place today can never find it again, making F1's own acceptance criterion untestable by a real person. Correctness dependency: removal must invalidate queryKeys.hubToday; both web Today mounts hold staleTime 120s, so today the address keeps rendering for two minutes after removal, which on an 'only you' surface reads as a privacy failure.

inventory.name: Add a place (signed-in address search + save)
inventory.hostSurface: Sheet over the Place tab and over Today. iOS has SavePlaceSheet.swift already but no entry point from these surfaces; Android has SavedPlacesApi and no signed-in write path at all; web has only the signed-out /start funnel.
inventory.purpose: Give 'Preview an address' and 'Save an address to see today here' a destination for a signed-in user who has no place — today both dead-end on Android.
inventory.contents: Address autocomplete, the selected suggestion, a single Save action, the privacy line ('A private bookmark for your account. Nobody else can see it.'), and on success a direct hand-off to Today. Reuses the existing SavedPlaces POST with expectedUserId.
states: geocode failure ('We couldn't find that address')
saved (sheet dismisses onto Today with the new chip)
duplicate of an existing saved place
entryPoints: Your places empty state and '+ Add'
Widget tap landing when there is no place
Place file address row when empty
inventory.visualization: A compact sheet: one focused field, suggestions as a plain list, one primary button, and a single privacy sentence — deliberately not a mini-funnel. No grades, no preview: this is 'bookmark it', and the reading happens on Today a second later.
inventory.uxNote: Adversarial walk found this as a hard dead end: the Place launch funnel is the SIGNED-OUT root, and Android's only saved-place write reads a pending draft from the signup flow. So a signed-in Android user with no place taps 'Preview an address' and reaches nothing. Routing those CTAs to 'Claim your address' instead would be worse — claiming is a much heavier promise than the copy makes.

inventory.name: Saved — Today now uses this address
inventory.hostSurface: Web: PendingPlaceSaver at /app/place?preview=<id> — as the success STATE of the save, not a route. iOS: Features/Place/Launch/PendingPlaceView.swift. Android: ui/screens/place/launch/PendingPlaceScreen.kt.
inventory.purpose: The one moment the user learns the save did anything. Say what changed, in one sentence, and hand them to Today.
inventory.contents: Title swap 'Keep this address handy' → 'Saved privately'. Body revised — today's 'a private bookmark… setting up a Home is a separate step' is now incomplete, because the save also sets Today and enables the briefing. Primary 'See Today', secondary 'Set up a Home', tertiary 'View saved places'. Carries the preview-lost recovery: when the local draft is unreadable, an inline address field with one-tap re-save instead of dropping to an empty Place.
states: preview lost / expired / different device — inline recovery
inventory.visualization: Two-state title with a single confirming glyph; three actions in strict weight order with the privacy sentence as a caption, never a second paragraph. The recovery state replaces the body with a focused address field and keeps the title, so a lost draft reads as 'type it again', not as an error page.
inventory.uxNote: Made a state rather than a dedicated route on web (it already is a route on both natives, which is fine).
